• EU enters winter with gas storage 75% full versus 83% a year earlier
  • European gas prices briefly touch €100/MWh for first time since December 2022
  • Commission starts dialogue with oil refineries to boost production

By Julia Payne

BRUSSELS, Oct 29 (Reuters) - EU energy ministers will meet on Thursday to discuss energy security ahead of the winter heating season as the wars in Iran, Ukraine and Yemen send oil and natural gas prices soaring.

Fighting has damaged refineries across the Middle East and Russia, and hampered oil and gas flows through vital shipping lanes in the Black Sea, Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz.

"We are in a very serious situation now. It does not look like we have a security of supply issue but I would warn against neglecting that," EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen told reporters on Wednesday. He said affordability was just as urgent an issue, arguing that available supply meant little to households and businesses that could not afford it.

The Commission began talks with European refineries on Wednesday to find ways to boost output, including through the possible easing of some technical specifications.

Western powers also agreed this month to accelerate the release of over 400 million barrels of emergency oil stocks after US pressure.

EU countries will also discuss a Commission proposal to cut electricity bills through tax and grid fee reforms, such as by taxing electricity at a lower rate than natural gas.

The EU is entering the winter heating season, with stocks at only 75% of available storage , versus 83% a year ago.

European wholesale gas prices briefly touched €100/MWh on Wednesday for the first time since December 2022 when Europe was reeling from the loss of most of its Russian pipeline gas supply. Prices have been rising as the conflict in the Middle East escalated, and are now trading at around triple pre-Iran war levels.

(Reporting by Julia Payne
Editing by Keith Weir)

Reports Outline Biological Factors Study Results from Guangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences (Preparation, Characterization, and Inhibitory Activity of Bacillus velezensis Crude Protein-based Composite Film Against the Fungal Pathogen of ...)

2026 OCT 28-- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at NewsRx Drug Daily-- Research findings on biological factors are discussed in a new report. According to news originating from Nanning, People' s Republic of China, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated," To develop a new biodegradable antifungal packaging material, this study employed a casting method to... 2026 OCT 28 (NewsRx) -- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at NewsRx Drug Daily -- Research findings on biological factors are discussed in a new report. According to news originating from Nanning, People's Republic of China, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated, "To develop a new biodegradable antifungal packaging material, this study employed a casting method to prepare composite films using carboxymethyl chitosan and konjac glucomannan as film forming materials, with the incorporating varying proportions of crude protein extract from Bacillus velezensis T9."

Our news editors obtained a quote from the research from Guangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences: "The morphology and chemical structure of the composite films were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). The physical, chemical, antifungal and preservation properties of the composite films were investigated. The results showed that the introduction of T9 crude protein increased the roughness and thickness of the composite films, but reduced its tensile strength, water vapor transmission rate, and light transmittance (P<0.05). All composite films exhibited good environmental biodegradability, with biodegradation rates exceeding 90% within 20 days. With increasing concentrations of T9 crude protein, the composite films demonstrated significantly enhanced antifungal activity against Apiospora arundinis (A. arundinis) and a markedly increased inhibition rate on 3-nitropropionic acid (3-NPA) mycotoxin synthesis (P<0.05). When the T9 crude protein addition reached 0.12% (KCB12 treatment), the inhibition zone diameter against A. arundinis reached 20.5 mm, the lesion length on sugarcane decreased by 51.03%~65.09% compared to the control group (CK), and no 3-NPA toxin was detected."

According to the news editors, the research concluded: "Furthermore, KCB12 treatment significantly reduced the weight loss rate (P<0.05), delayed the decrease in sugarcane juice pH, and maintained higher levels of soluble solids and sucrose content in sugarcane during storage. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the practical application of crude protein-based composite films from Bacillus velezensis T9 to control mycotoxin contamination and preserve the postharvest quality of sugarcane."

For more information on this research see: Preparation, Characterization, and Inhibitory Activity of Bacillus velezensis Crude Protein-based Composite Film Against the Fungal Pathogen of Moldy Sugarcane. Shipin gongye ke-ji , 2026,47(20):336-346. The publisher for Shipin gongye ke-ji is The editorial department of Science and Technology of Food Industry.

A free version of this journal article is available at https://doi.org/10.13386/j.issn1002-0306.2025090155 .

Our news journalists report that additional information may be obtained by contacting Wenyan JIANG, Agro-products Quality Safety and Testing Technology Research Institute, Guangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Nanning 530007, People's Republic of China. Additional authors for this research include Xuelian LIANG, Huiling LI, Tianshun WANG, Wei CHEN, Haijun WANG, Weifan LU, Yuning WEI, Qifeng ZHOU, Jie LIAO.

(Our reports deliver fact-based news of research and discoveries from around the world.)

Israelis are deep in political uncertainty as they await final election results

Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family have landed in Miami after fleeing Brazil

Legendary labor organizer Dolores Huerta has died

Cornell University faculty have voted against delaying a proposed no-confidence resolution in the university's administration until an independent investigation into its handling of sexual assault allegations is completed

Drew Rasmussen will start for Tampa Bay on three days' rest in Game 5 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, trying to stave off elimination for the Rays

Oct 29 (Reuters) - Google parent Alphabet's results could spark a rocky ride for Asian markets after a subdued offshore session on Wednesday, with the Federal Reserve holding interest rates steady as widely expected.

AI-spending concerns are likely to be revived as Alphabet shares fell 10% in extended trading after the company missed Wall Street profit and revenue expectations while its negative free cash flow reached $9.07 billion, confounding analysts' expectations it would nearly break even. Nasdaq futures are down 1.1% early on Thursday.

The regional data schedule is light. Results from South Korean chipmaker Samsung and a 2.6% after-hours rise in Microsoft shares on forecast-beating results may offer some respite from AI-spending fears.

The Fed left rates steady at 3.75%-4.00%, upgraded its assessment of the economy and acknowledged inflation remained elevated, while signalling it would await further data before making a decision in December. The probability of a rate hike in December rose to 82% from 75% on Tuesday.

US crude futures closed 2% higher on concerns over supply disruptions following an attack on a Saudi Arabia refinery and worries about a flare-up in the Middle East conflict following next week's US midterm elections. The prospect of Benjamin Netanyahu remaining Israel's caretaker prime minister after an inconclusive Israeli election also supported prices.

Dow +0.19%, S&P 500 +0.28%, Nasdaq +0.27% on the steady Fed. Treasury yields bear-steepened on inflation concerns; 2yr unchanged at 4.735%, 10yr +5bps to 5.045% and 30 yr +6.1bps to 5.361%.

The U.S. dollar index =USDshed 0.2%; EUR +0.3%, JPY and CHF +0.1%, GBP +0.15% with the UK budget taken in stride, CNH steady, AUD +0.4% on hawkish comments from the Reserve Bank of Australia, CAD +0.4% after the Bank of Canada raised rates by 25 basis points but NZD -1% after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand unexpectedly held rates. Bitcoin +0.5%.

Gold +0.2% and copper +0.3% on the steady Fed.

4.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. It is Mexico's largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261028:nNRA2h.html_limpio: Fomento Económico Mexicano (Femsa) ha adquirido el 100% de Caffenio como parte de su estrategia para impulsar categorías de alto margen y aumentar el tráfico en las tiendas Oxxo a través del negocio del café. Durante la conferencia de resultados del tercer trimestre, la dirección de Femsa anunció la compra de la participación restante en la empresa de cafeterías, lo que permitirá generar eficiencias en los gastos corporativos, alinear incentivos operativos y fortalecer la propuesta de valor en las tiendas. El CEO de Femsa, José Antonio Fernández Garza, destacó la competencia con otros jugadores que deben pagar regalías de franquicia, y reafirmó su intención de seguir abriendo locales de café de autoservicio. Aunque no se revelaron los términos financieros de la transacción, Femsa ha ido aumentando su participación en Caffenio desde 2012. Caffenio opera alrededor de 300 puntos de venta de autoservicio, que han ganado popularidad entre los consumidores. Además, se enfatizó que este formato independiente servirá como un laboratorio de desarrollo de productos, impulsando la innovación en bebidas de café y alimentos para Oxxo en México y Sudamérica.

India, Oct. 29 -- Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday after he refused to concede the election to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and fled the country. In a circuitous journey, Bolsonaro left for Argentina on Tuesday with his wife and two daughters, then travelled to Ecuador, according to Argentina officials and flight data. The 45-year-old senator, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, visited the White House in May, and the Trump administration approved US visas for him and his family this week. Bolsonaro is under investigation by Brazil's Supreme Court, accused of corruption, money laundering and tax evasion. The court had ordered him to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports by Tuesday.P10 Published by HT Digital Content Services with permission from HT Pune. MEXICAN STOCK REPORT

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Solvency of Arca Continental

Debt to Equity Ratio of Arca Continental for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.36; a deterioration from 0.28 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Debt to Assets Ratio of Arca Continental for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.20; a deterioration from 0.17 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Altman-Z score of Arca Continental

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Arca Continental with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Arca Continental scores a Z = 0.95 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025]; an improvement from 0.95 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and a deterioration from 0.96 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Liquidity of Arca Continental

Acid Test Ratio of Arca Continental for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.88; a deterioration from 1.04 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 1.2 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. This change in current ratio was driven by

- A decrease in current assets of MX$9.7 billion (or 13.1%) from the previous quarter and MX$3.3 billion (or 4.8%) from year ago to MX$64.4 billion.

- A decrease in current liabilities of MX$1.4 billion (or 2.5%) from the previous quarter and an increase of MX$11 billion (or 24.1%) from year ago to MX$56.4 billion.

Piotroski F-Score of Arca Continental

Arca Continental has achieved a high Piotroski F-Score of 7 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025], indicating solid financial health and operational efficiency. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. Despite one data point being unavailable, the adjusted score provides a reliable indication that Arca Continental is not only generating solid earnings and cash flow but also managing its balance sheet prudently positioning it well for sustained growth and investor confidence.

Free Cash Flow (FCF) of Arca Continental

Free Cash Flow (FCF) growth is a fundamental risk metric that reflects a company's capacity to generate surplus cash from its core operations after capital expenditures. This metric directly influences a firm's liquidity, self-sufficiency, and ability to manage obligations without external funding.

A positive and rising FCF generally implies operational efficiency, strong margins, and disciplined investment - all of which reduce financial risk. However, declining or negative FCF growth, particularly over consecutive quarters, may indicate emerging liquidity stress, unsustainable capital outlays, or revenue compression. Monitoring FCF growth helps assess a company's financial flexibility, its vulnerability to external shocks, and the likelihood of financing constraints.

Arca Continental Free Cash Flow for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is MX$8.2 billion; representing a 144.26% increase from MX$3.4 billion in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and a 30.12% decrease compared to MX$11.7 billion in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Debt to Assets Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.27; a deterioration from 0.16 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Altman-Z score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste scores a Z = 0.84 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025]; a deterioration from 1.1 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 2.21 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Liquidity of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste

Current Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 1.84; a deterioration from 4.36 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 4.36 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. This change in current ratio was driven by

- A decrease in current assets of MX$177.3 million (or 0.7%) from the previous quarter and MX$177.3 million (or 0.7%) from year ago to MX$25.5 billion.

- An increase in current liabilities of MX$7.9 billion (or 134.6%) from the previous quarter and MX$7.9 billion (or 134.6%) from year ago to MX$13.8 billion.

Piotroski F-Score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste has posted a mid-range Piotroski F-Score of 6 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025], indicating a blend of strengths and weaknesses in its financial fundamentals. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. Despite one data point being unavailable, the adjusted score provides a reliable indication that Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

Free Cash Flow (FCF) of Grupo Mexico

Free Cash Flow (FCF) growth is a fundamental risk metric that reflects a company's capacity to generate surplus cash from its core operations after capital expenditures. This metric directly influences a firm's liquidity, self-sufficiency, and ability to manage obligations without external funding.

A positive and rising FCF generally implies operational efficiency, strong margins, and disciplined investment - all of which reduce financial risk. However, declining or negative FCF growth, particularly over consecutive quarters, may indicate emerging liquidity stress, unsustainable capital outlays, or revenue compression. Monitoring FCF growth helps assess a company's financial flexibility, its vulnerability to external shocks, and the likelihood of financing constraints.

Grupo Mexico Free Cash Flow for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is $805.7 million; representing a 140.47% increase from $335 million in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and a 31.28% decrease compared to $1.2 billion in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Fomento Económico Mexicano (Femsa), the retail and bottling conglomerate, announced that it has acquired 100% ownership of Caffenio as part of its strategy to accelerate high-margin categories and drive traffic to Oxxo stores through the coffee business.

During the third-quarter results conference, Femsa's management revealed that it purchased the remaining stake it did not own in the coffee shop company. This transaction will allow them to generate efficiencies in corporate expenses, align operational incentives, and strengthen the in-store value proposition.

"We compete against players that have to pay many franchise royalties; we are very happy with that competition, and we will continue to open self-service coffee locations," said José Antonio Fernández Garza, CEO of Femsa, to analysts and investors.

The financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed; Femsa has gradually increased its stake in Caffenio since 2012. The company was originally founded by the Díaz family in the northern part of the country.

In addition to supplying the hot and prepared beverage infrastructure for Oxxo, Caffenio independently operates around 300 self-service (drive-thru) outlets. Company executives noted that these outlets have developed a "cult following" among consumers, resulting in constant lines of customers.

Moreover, Femsa executives emphasized that the independent format will also serve as a product development laboratory.

"Caffenio's self-service locations are truly a very good and interesting source of innovation. They are a much smaller business, almost venture capital in the way they test and try new things... so I believe it will also be a very interesting engine for bringing novelties to Oxxo Mexico and to South America in everything related to coffee beverages and even food," said the finance executive, Martín Arias, during the conference.

The Federal Reserve of the United States (Fed) kept the benchmark interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, in a decision that was not unanimous, maintaining the range at 3.75% to 4% annually, amidst higher inflation and the possibility of another increase in December . Experts detail how this could impact Argentina, where the country risk and financing costs are expected to remain high.

This decision aligned with market expectations, although two officials supported a new rate hike of 25 basis points. The other 10 officials voted in favor of maintaining the rates, which was the prevailing decision.

"The strength of the economy and the persistence of inflation keep open the possibility of another monetary adjustment in December," summarized Research for Traders.

They believe that this decision represents a pause in the monetary tightening cycle, but not necessarily the end of it.

"The Fed presented a more favorable assessment of economic activity , now considering it to be growing at a strong pace. It highlighted the resilience of consumption, the robustness of investment, and productivity, while noting that employment growth is keeping pace with the labor force and that unemployment remains relatively stable," analysts observed.

In concrete terms, inflation remains elevated, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for September at 3.7% year-on-year, still far from the Fed's target of 2%. The statement incorporated the need to assess additional information before determining the appropriate level of rates, without committing to a new increase in the next meeting.

Impact of the Fed's Decision on Argentina

In Argentina, maintaining high interest rates complicates the reduction of country risk, meaning financing costs will remain high. This affects national bonds .

According to Pablo Lazzati , CEO of Insider Finance, "for Argentina, the main impact is on bonds and country risk . With risk-free rates close to 5%, international investors demand higher yields on the debt of higher-risk countries, limiting the compression margin."

Currently, country risk stands at around 742 points , following a rebound in recent days, but it remains far from the 600 points recorded at the beginning of the month.

"I don't believe this decision will have a direct impact on Argentina, as it would maintain the same conditions seen in the market . What it does is fail to contribute to reducing country risk, and therefore, the yield on Argentine bonds would remain at this level and it wouldn't help prices to continue rising," summarizes Esteban Castro .

Thus, for Argentina, the effect is mainly felt through the cost of capital.

"With high rates in the United States, investors remain more demanding in taking on emerging market risk, which reflects in financing costs, bonds, and country risk, at a time when the country seeks to consolidate its return to international markets," says Julián Colombo , General Director of Bitso Argentina.

He adds: "If the pause is confirmed as the beginning of a longer period of stable rates, the market could gain predictability. However, if the Fed keeps the door open for new increases, we should expect global caution to persist in the coming months."

In concrete terms, the increase in financing rates affects costs for companies and, consequently, the price of their stocks.

"The Fed's benchmark interest rate directly impacts the public and private financing available for Argentina . It not only affects the availability of funds but also the prevailing rates for variable rate borrowings, such as SOFR. Domestically, rates are somewhat more decoupled, influenced by other variables such as dollar deposits in the system, the trade balance, the peso rate, and expected inflation," claims Martin Lepiane, partner at MHR.

Impact on the Dollar

On the foreign exchange front, a strong global dollar pressures emerging market currencies, including the real, and "this translates to the local exchange rate , which remains stable within the band established by the Central Bank but with a cash with liquidation that has already diverged from the official rate," warns Lazzati.

Regarding inflation, he states that the effect is indirect , as if the exchange rate moves more quickly, it could translate to the prices of tradable goods, although with the current band in place and the BCRA purchasing reserves, "we do not see a significant impact in the short term."

Investment Suggestions from Argentina Following the Fed's Decision

Regarding investments, with current international interest rates, experts from the City recommend which stocks and bonds to consider.

"For investors, we recommend not chasing duration in this context. In dollar-denominated bonds, we prefer the short-term segment, such as bonar and global bonds maturing in 2029 and 2030, and negotiable obligations (ON) from top-tier companies, which offer attractive yields with lower sensitivity to rates," states Lazzati.

In pesos, he indicates that he maintains a mix of CER-indexed (inflation-adjusted) and fixed rates with a portion in dollar-linked assets for coverage, as it adjusts based on the movement of the official exchange rate.

On the equity side, recommendations suggest positioning in foreign companies through Argentine Deposit Certificates (CEDEARs).

"In CEDEARs, a strong dollar and high rates favor companies with cash and solid results compared to those that rely on financing, which is why we prefer to be selective and stagger purchases," concludes Lazzati.

SECTION 1 CORPORATE PROFILE

1.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Fitch Ratings-Monterrey-28 October 2026:

Fitch Ratings afirmó las calificaciones internacionales de riesgo emisor (IDR; issuer default rating) de largo plazo en monedas extranjera y local de Grupo Financiero Banorte, S.A.B. de C.V. (GFNorte) y Banco Mercantil del Norte, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Banorte) en ‘BBB-’, como resultado de la afirmación de la calificación de viabilidad (VR; viability rating) de Banorte en ‘bbb-’. Las IDR de corto plazo en monedas extranjera y local se afirmaron en ‘F3’ y la calificación de soporte del gobierno (GSR; government support rating) de Banorte se afirmó en ‘bb+’. La Perspectiva de las IDR de largo plazo es Positiva.

Fitch también afirmó las calificaciones nacionales de largo y corto plazo de Banorte, Arrendadora y Factor Banorte, S.A. de C.V., SOFOM, E.R., Grupo Financiero Banorte (AyF Banorte), Casa de Bolsa Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Grupo Financiero Banorte (CB Banorte) y Almacenadora Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Organización Auxiliar del Crédito, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Almacenadora Banorte) en ‘AAA(mex)’ y ‘F1+(mex)’, respectivamente. La Perspectiva de todas las calificaciones en escala nacional de largo plazo es Estable. Al final de este comunicado se presenta la lista completa de acciones de calificación.

FACTORES CLAVE DE CALIFICACIÓN

Entorno Operativo Estable: La puntuación del entorno operativo (EO) se afirmó en ‘bb+’, con tendencia estable, y se encuentra por debajo de su puntuación implícita de ‘bbb’. Las condiciones operativas buenas para los bancos mexicanos se mantienen, aunque el desempeño económico moderado continúa influyendo en la capacidad de los bancos para generar negocios. El PIB per cápita estimado de México para 2026 es de USD16,234, mientras el percentil del índice de riesgo operativo (ORI) de Fitch se ubicó en 45.8% en octubre de 2026, lo que respalda la puntuación implícita de ‘bbb’. Fitch ajustó la puntuación implícita del EO considerando el desempeño económico como un factor negativo.

Perspectiva Positiva: La Perspectiva Positiva refleja las mejoras continuas en los perfiles de negocio y financiero de Banorte, que Fitch espera se mantengan. Estas incluyen un indicador de utilidad operativa sobre activos ponderados por riesgo (APR) superior a 4.75%, un indicador de capital común nivel 1 (CET 1; common equity tier 1) cercano a 14% y una reducción gradual de la exposición al sector público. De sostenerse estas mejoras, podrían conducir a una acción de calificación positiva durante los próximos 12 meses.

Desempeño Sólido Impulsa las Calificaciones: Las IDR y calificaciones nacionales de Banorte están determinadas por su VR de ‘bbb-’. La VR refleja el perfil de negocio consolidado del banco, su sólido marco de riesgos, así como su buen desempeño financiero a lo largo del ciclo económico. Fitch afirmó la puntuación del perfil de negocio de Banorte en ‘bbb-’ con Perspectiva Positiva. La agencia considera que Banorte continuará consolidando su posición de liderazgo en México mediante ganancias de participación de mercado y una mayor brecha frente a sus competidores más cercanos. El ingreso operativo total (IOT) promedio de Banorte durante el período de cuatro años comprendido entre 2022 y 2025 fue de USD6,500 millones, cifra que ha superado gradualmente la de sus pares más cercanos.

Gestión Prudente de Riesgos: Fitch afirmó la puntuación del perfil de riesgo de Banorte en ‘bbb-’ con Perspectiva Positiva. Esta evaluación refleja los sólidos y consistentes estándares de originación de crédito del banco a lo largo de los ciclos económicos, así como su robusto marco de control de riesgos, que Fitch considera acorde con su perfil de negocio.

El crecimiento del balance ha sido prudente y se ha respaldado de manera consistente en métricas sólidas de capitalización y amplia cobertura por garantías. Estos factores mitigan las mayores concentraciones de Banorte frente a alguno de sus pares. En opinión de Fitch, el perfil de riesgo consistente de Banorte, junto con una infraestructura robusta de riesgos, garantiza un control eficaz de la calidad crediticia y un monitoreo adecuado de los distintos riesgos. Una tendencia descendente sostenida en su exposición al soberano mexicana sería considerada favorablemente por Fitch y podría respaldar una mejora en la evaluación del perfil de riesgo.

Calidad de Activos Sólida: La evaluación de calidad de activos de Banorte de ‘bbb-’ refleja métricas ampliamente estables durante los últimos cinco años. Los créditos en etapa 3 representaron 1.5% de los créditos brutos en el segundo trimestre de 2026 (2T26), frente a un promedio de 1.1%, en los últimos cuatro años debido a una exposición crediticia comercial aislada desde el 3T25 y a la consolidación de la cartera de crédito de Tarjetas del Futuro. Sin embargo, las métricas de cartera en etapa 3 (NPL; non-performing loans ratio) en todos los segmentos crediticios se han mantenido estables y se comparan favorablemente con los de sus pares. Fitch espera que el índice de NPL retorne a niveles históricos y que la puntuación de calidad de activos continúe respaldada por los estándares prudentes de originación de Banorte y su elevada cobertura de garantías, factores que deberían favorecer las perspectivas de recuperación.

Rentabilidad Sólida y Resiliente: La evaluación de Fitch de ‘bbb-’ para ganancias y rentabilidad de Banorte refleja su rentabilidad operativa consistente, respaldada por ingresos netos por intereses resilientes, costos crediticios moderados y eficiencias operativas. El indicador de utilidad operativa sobre APR fue de 6.2% al 2T26, frente a un promedio de 5.9% entre 2022 y 2025. Las métricas de rentabilidad de Banorte comparan favorablemente con sus pares, y el banco se ubica entre las instituciones bancarias mexicanas de mayor tamaño más rentables. Fitch espera que las métricas de rentabilidad subyacente se mantengan cercanas a 6%.

Capitalización Sólida: La evaluación de puntuación de Fitch de ‘bbb-’ para capitalización y apalancamiento de Banorte refleja métricas robustas de capital y amplios colchones por encima de los requerimientos regulatorios locales. El indicador CET1 del banco se situó en 12.6% al 2T26, frente a 14% en el 2T25 debido al pago de dividendos. Fitch espera que el índice CET1 se recupere a 13% o más mediante la generación de utilidades del banco.

Los instrumentos híbridos con capacidad de absorción de pérdidas, principalmente instrumentos de capital adicional de nivel 1 (AT1), respaldaron un índice de capital total de 21.5% al 2T26, lo que Fitch considera positivo. La agencia espera que el capital de Banorte permanezca suficiente para absorber el crecimiento esperado de los créditos y respaldar distribuciones de dividendos consistentes.

Perfil de Fondeo y Liquidez Mejorado: La puntuación de ‘bbb-’ para el factor de fondeo y liquidez de Banorte refleja mejoras estructurales en su mezcla de fondeo y en sus costos de financiamiento. El indicador de créditos sobre depósitos del banco fue de 103.5% al 2T26, frente a un promedio de 102.0% entre 2022 y 2025. Su coeficiente de fondeo estable neto fue de 132% en el 2T26. El aumento de los depósitos a la vista constituye un componente clave de la estrategia de fondeo de Banorte; estos representaron 67.4% del total de depósitos de clientes al 2T26 y muestran una tendencia hacia niveles similares a los de sus pares.

SENSIBILIDAD DE CALIFICACIÓN Factores que Podrían, Individual o Colectivamente, Conducir a una Acción de Calificación Negativa/Baja

--la Perspectiva podría revisarse a Estable si Banorte no logra sostener las mejoras en sus perfiles de negocio y financiero;

--las VR e IDR de Banorte son sensibles a una acción de calificación sobre las calificaciones soberanas de México o a una revisión a la baja de la evaluación de Fitch sobre el EO;

--las calificaciones de Banorte podrían bajar si el desempeño financiero se deteriora de manera sostenida, con un indicador de utilidad operativa sobre APR inferior a 2.5%, un indicador CET1 sobre APR por debajo de 12% y un debilitamiento de la evaluación del perfil de riesgo de Fitch que denote un deterioro en la calidad de activos;

--un aumento significativo de la exposición del banco al soberano también podría provocar una baja de la VR en el mismo nivel que la calificación soberana;

--las calificaciones nacionales de Banorte reflejarán cualquier cambio en las relatividades crediticias locales. La Perspectiva podría revisarse a Estable si Banorte no logra sostener las mejoras en sus perfiles de negocio y financiero.

Factores que Podrían, Individual o Colectivamente, Conducir a una Acción de Calificación Positiva/Alza

--las VR e IDR podrían subir si se eleva la calificación soberana y Fitch revisa al alza su evaluación del EO, mientras el banco mantiene perfiles de negocio y financiero muy sólidos;

--un crecimiento sostenido del IOT, acompañado de un desempeño financiero sólido y consistente, específicamente un indicador de utilidad operativa sobre APR superior a 4.75%; índices de CET1/APR y capital total cercanos o superiores a 14% y 21%, respectivamente; métricas de calidad de activos en niveles razonables, y una reducción de la exposición al soberano mexicano, reflejada en una razón de deuda soberana a CET1 cercana o inferior a 2x, podría respaldar una acción positiva;

--las calificaciones nacionales de Banorte no tienen potencial de mejora debido a que ya se ubican en el nivel más alto de la escala nacional;

OTRAS CALIFICACIONES DE DEUDA: FACTORES CLAVE DE CALIFICACIÓN

Deuda Sénior Quirografaria de Banorte: Las calificaciones de la deuda sénior quirografaria local están alineadas con la calificación nacional de largo plazo de Banorte de ‘AAA(mex)’, dado que la probabilidad de incumplimiento de las notas es la misma que la del emisor y se esperan recuperaciones promedio.

Banorte Clasificado como D-SIB: La GSR de Banorte de ‘bb+’ refleja su elevada importancia sistémica. El banco está definido como un banco de importancia sistémica local (D-SIB). Debido a su participación de mercado y amplia interconexión dentro del sistema financiero, Fitch considera elevada la propensión de las autoridades a proporcionar apoyo para evitar riesgos de contagio.

Al 2T26, la participación de mercado de Banorte en depósitos de clientes fue de 14%, lo que lo posiciona como el segundo banco del sistema. Sin embargo, Fitch considera que la probabilidad de apoyo para Banorte es menor que para otros bancos grandes vinculados a políticas públicas debido a la propiedad privada de Banorte.

OTRAS CALIFICACIONES DE DEUDA: SENSIBILIDAD DE CALIFICACIÓN

Calificaciones de Deuda

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación negativa/baja:

--una baja de la calificación de la deuda sénior de Banorte reflejaría cualquier baja en las calificaciones nacionales del emisor.

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación positiva/alza:

--la calificación de la deuda sénior de Banorte no tiene potencial de mejora debido a que es la más alta de la escala nacional.

Calificación de Soporte Gubernamental

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación negativa/baja:

--la GSR de Banorte podría bajar si la capacidad del soberano para brindar apoyo al banco se debilita como resultado de una baja de la calificación soberana, o si disminuye la propensión del soberano a proporcionar dicho apoyo.

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación positiva/alza:

-- un alza de la GSR de Banorte es posible en caso de un alza de la calificación soberana que coincida con un fortalecimiento de la capacidad y propensión del soberano para brindar apoyo al banco.

SUBSIDIARIAS Y AFILIADAS: FACTORES CLAVE DE CALIFICACIÓN

Calificaciones de GFNorte Igualadas con las de Banorte: Fitch considera que el riesgo de incumplimiento de GFNorte es sustancialmente el mismo que el de Banorte debido a la dependencia de GFNorte de los flujos de dividendos provenientes del banco y del valor de su inversión en este. Las calificaciones de GFNorte también reflejan, con alta relevancia, su bajo índice de doble apalancamiento, medido como inversiones en subsidiarias respecto del patrimonio tangible.

El índice de doble apalancamiento fue de 98.2% en el 2T26, frente a 96.4% en el 2T25, y se mantuvo muy por debajo del umbral de 120% de Fitch.

El Soporte Sustenta las Calificaciones Nacionales de las Subsidiarias: Las calificaciones nacionales de CB Banorte, AyF Banorte y Almacenadora Banorte reflejan el perfil crediticio de su compañía controladora, GFNorte, que a su vez está determinado por Banorte, la principal entidad operativa del grupo. Fitch incorpora el soporte explícito que se esperaría que el grupo financiero proporcionara a estas entidades, dados sus roles en la estrategia de diversificación de negocios del grupo y la obligación legal de GFNorte de respaldar a sus subsidiarias.

SUBSIDIARIAS Y AFILIADAS: SENSIBILIDAD DE CALIFICACIÓN

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación negativa/baja:

-las IDR de GFNorte podrían bajar si se produce un aumento significativo y sostenido del doble apalancamiento por encima de 120%. Esto daría lugar a calificaciones un nivel por debajo de las IDR de Banorte;

--cualquier movimiento negativo en las calificaciones de las subsidiarias no bancarias de GFNorte derivaría de una acción negativa sobre las calificaciones nacionales de Banorte;

--un cambio en la importancia estratégica para el grupo y el banco de las subsidiarias no bancarias de GFNorte podría afectar sus calificaciones.

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación positiva/alza:

--un alza de las IDR de GFNorte resultaría de cualquier cambio positivo en la VR de Banorte;

--las calificaciones de las subsidiarias no bancarias de GFNorte se encuentran en el nivel más alto de la escala nacional; por lo tanto, no existe posibilidad de un alza de estas calificaciones.

AJUSTES A LA CALIFICACIÓN VR

La puntuación del EO de ‘bb+’ se ubica por debajo de la puntuación implícita de la categoría ‘bbb’ debido al siguiente motivo de ajuste: desempeño económico (negativo).

La puntuación de calidad de activos de ‘bbb-’ se ubica por encima de la puntuación implícita de la categoría ‘bb’ debido al siguiente motivo de ajuste: garantías y reservas (positivo).

La puntuación de capitalización y apalancamiento de ‘bbb-’ se ubica por encima de la puntuación implícita de la categoría ‘bb’ debido al siguiente motivo de ajuste: apalancamiento y cálculo de riesgos (positivo).

La puntuación de fondeo y liquidez de ‘bbb-’ se ubica por encima de la puntuación implícita de la categoría ‘bb’ debido al siguiente motivo de ajuste: estructura de depósitos (positivo).

A menos que se indique lo contrario en esta sección, el nivel más alto de puntaje de relevancia crediticia ambiental, social y de gobernanza (ESG; environmental, social and governance) es de ‘3’. Un puntaje de ‘3’ significa que los aspectos ESG son neutrales para el crédito o tienen un impacto crediticio mínimo en la entidad, ya sea debido a la naturaleza de los mismos o a la forma en que son gestionados por la entidad. Fitch Ratings-Monterrey-28 October 2026:

Fitch Ratings afirmó las calificaciones internacionales de riesgo emisor (IDR; issuer default rating) de largo plazo en monedas extranjera y local de Grupo Financiero Banorte, S.A.B. de C.V. (GFNorte) y Banco Mercantil del Norte, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Banorte) en ‘BBB-’, como resultado de la afirmación de la calificación de viabilidad (VR; viability rating) de Banorte en ‘bbb-’. Las IDR de corto plazo en monedas extranjera y local se afirmaron en ‘F3’ y la calificación de soporte del gobierno (GSR; government support rating) de Banorte se afirmó en ‘bb+’. La Perspectiva de las IDR de largo plazo es Positiva.

Fitch también afirmó las calificaciones nacionales de largo y corto plazo de Banorte, Arrendadora y Factor Banorte, S.A. de C.V., SOFOM, E.R., Grupo Financiero Banorte (AyF Banorte), Casa de Bolsa Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Grupo Financiero Banorte (CB Banorte) y Almacenadora Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Organización Auxiliar del Crédito, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Almacenadora Banorte) en ‘AAA(mex)’ y ‘F1+(mex)’, respectivamente. La Perspectiva de todas las calificaciones en escala nacional de largo plazo es Estable. Al final de este comunicado se presenta la lista completa de acciones de calificación.

FACTORES CLAVE DE CALIFICACIÓN

Entorno Operativo Estable: La puntuación del entorno operativo (EO) se afirmó en ‘bb+’, con tendencia estable, y se encuentra por debajo de su puntuación implícita de ‘bbb’. Las condiciones operativas buenas para los bancos mexicanos se mantienen, aunque el desempeño económico moderado continúa influyendo en la capacidad de los bancos para generar negocios. El PIB per cápita estimado de México para 2026 es de USD16,234, mientras el percentil del índice de riesgo operativo (ORI) de Fitch se ubicó en 45.8% en octubre de 2026, lo que respalda la puntuación implícita de ‘bbb’. Fitch ajustó la puntuación implícita del EO considerando el desempeño económico como un factor negativo.

Perspectiva Positiva: La Perspectiva Positiva refleja las mejoras continuas en los perfiles de negocio y financiero de Banorte, que Fitch espera se mantengan. Estas incluyen un indicador de utilidad operativa sobre activos ponderados por riesgo (APR) superior a 4.75%, un indicador de capital común nivel 1 (CET 1; common equity tier 1) cercano a 14% y una reducción gradual de la exposición al sector público. De sostenerse estas mejoras, podrían conducir a una acción de calificación positiva durante los próximos 12 meses.

Desempeño Sólido Impulsa las Calificaciones: Las IDR y calificaciones nacionales de Banorte están determinadas por su VR de ‘bbb-’. La VR refleja el perfil de negocio consolidado del banco, su sólido marco de riesgos, así como su buen desempeño financiero a lo largo del ciclo económico. Fitch afirmó la puntuación del perfil de negocio de Banorte en ‘bbb-’ con Perspectiva Positiva. La agencia considera que Banorte continuará consolidando su posición de liderazgo en México mediante ganancias de participación de mercado y una mayor brecha frente a sus competidores más cercanos. El ingreso operativo total (IOT) promedio de Banorte durante el período de cuatro años comprendido entre 2022 y 2025 fue de USD6,500 millones, cifra que ha superado gradualmente la de sus pares más cercanos.

Gestión Prudente de Riesgos: Fitch afirmó la puntuación del perfil de riesgo de Banorte en ‘bbb-’ con Perspectiva Positiva. Esta evaluación refleja los sólidos y consistentes estándares de originación de crédito del banco a lo largo de los ciclos económicos, así como su robusto marco de control de riesgos, que Fitch considera acorde con su perfil de negocio.

El crecimiento del balance ha sido prudente y se ha respaldado de manera consistente en métricas sólidas de capitalización y amplia cobertura por garantías. Estos factores mitigan las mayores concentraciones de Banorte frente a alguno de sus pares. En opinión de Fitch, el perfil de riesgo consistente de Banorte, junto con una infraestructura robusta de riesgos, garantiza un control eficaz de la calidad crediticia y un monitoreo adecuado de los distintos riesgos. Una tendencia descendente sostenida en su exposición al soberano mexicana sería considerada favorablemente por Fitch y podría respaldar una mejora en la evaluación del perfil de riesgo.

Calidad de Activos Sólida: La evaluación de calidad de activos de Banorte de ‘bbb-’ refleja métricas ampliamente estables durante los últimos cinco años. Los créditos en etapa 3 representaron 1.5% de los créditos brutos en el segundo trimestre de 2026 (2T26), frente a un promedio de 1.1%, en los últimos cuatro años debido a una exposición crediticia comercial aislada desde el 3T25 y a la consolidación de la cartera de crédito de Tarjetas del Futuro. Sin embargo, las métricas de cartera en etapa 3 (NPL; non-performing loans ratio) en todos los segmentos crediticios se han mantenido estables y se comparan favorablemente con los de sus pares. Fitch espera que el índice de NPL retorne a niveles históricos y que la puntuación de calidad de activos continúe respaldada por los estándares prudentes de originación de Banorte y su elevada cobertura de garantías, factores que deberían favorecer las perspectivas de recuperación.

Rentabilidad Sólida y Resiliente: La evaluación de Fitch de ‘bbb-’ para ganancias y rentabilidad de Banorte refleja su rentabilidad operativa consistente, respaldada por ingresos netos por intereses resilientes, costos crediticios moderados y eficiencias operativas. El indicador de utilidad operativa sobre APR fue de 6.2% al 2T26, frente a un promedio de 5.9% entre 2022 y 2025. Las métricas de rentabilidad de Banorte comparan favorablemente con sus pares, y el banco se ubica entre las instituciones bancarias mexicanas de mayor tamaño más rentables. Fitch espera que las métricas de rentabilidad subyacente se mantengan cercanas a 6%.

Capitalización Sólida: La evaluación de puntuación de Fitch de ‘bbb-’ para capitalización y apalancamiento de Banorte refleja métricas robustas de capital y amplios colchones por encima de los requerimientos regulatorios locales. El indicador CET1 del banco se situó en 12.6% al 2T26, frente a 14% en el 2T25 debido al pago de dividendos. Fitch espera que el índice CET1 se recupere a 13% o más mediante la generación de utilidades del banco.

Los instrumentos híbridos con capacidad de absorción de pérdidas, principalmente instrumentos de capital adicional de nivel 1 (AT1), respaldaron un índice de capital total de 21.5% al 2T26, lo que Fitch considera positivo. La agencia espera que el capital de Banorte permanezca suficiente para absorber el crecimiento esperado de los créditos y respaldar distribuciones de dividendos consistentes.

Perfil de Fondeo y Liquidez Mejorado: La puntuación de ‘bbb-’ para el factor de fondeo y liquidez de Banorte refleja mejoras estructurales en su mezcla de fondeo y en sus costos de financiamiento. El indicador de créditos sobre depósitos del banco fue de 103.5% al 2T26, frente a un promedio de 102.0% entre 2022 y 2025. Su coeficiente de fondeo estable neto fue de 132% en el 2T26. El aumento de los depósitos a la vista constituye un componente clave de la estrategia de fondeo de Banorte; estos representaron 67.4% del total de depósitos de clientes al 2T26 y muestran una tendencia hacia niveles similares a los de sus pares.

SENSIBILIDAD DE CALIFICACIÓN Factores que Podrían, Individual o Colectivamente, Conducir a una Acción de Calificación Negativa/Baja

--la Perspectiva podría revisarse a Estable si Banorte no logra sostener las mejoras en sus perfiles de negocio y financiero;

--las VR e IDR de Banorte son sensibles a una acción de calificación sobre las calificaciones soberanas de México o a una revisión a la baja de la evaluación de Fitch sobre el EO;

--las calificaciones de Banorte podrían bajar si el desempeño financiero se deteriora de manera sostenida, con un indicador de utilidad operativa sobre APR inferior a 2.5%, un indicador CET1 sobre APR por debajo de 12% y un debilitamiento de la evaluación del perfil de riesgo de Fitch que denote un deterioro en la calidad de activos;

--un aumento significativo de la exposición del banco al soberano también podría provocar una baja de la VR en el mismo nivel que la calificación soberana;

--las calificaciones nacionales de Banorte reflejarán cualquier cambio en las relatividades crediticias locales. La Perspectiva podría revisarse a Estable si Banorte no logra sostener las mejoras en sus perfiles de negocio y financiero.

Factores que Podrían, Individual o Colectivamente, Conducir a una Acción de Calificación Positiva/Alza

--las VR e IDR podrían subir si se eleva la calificación soberana y Fitch revisa al alza su evaluación del EO, mientras el banco mantiene perfiles de negocio y financiero muy sólidos;

--un crecimiento sostenido del IOT, acompañado de un desempeño financiero sólido y consistente, específicamente un indicador de utilidad operativa sobre APR superior a 4.75%; índices de CET1/APR y capital total cercanos o superiores a 14% y 21%, respectivamente; métricas de calidad de activos en niveles razonables, y una reducción de la exposición al soberano mexicano, reflejada en una razón de deuda soberana a CET1 cercana o inferior a 2x, podría respaldar una acción positiva;

--las calificaciones nacionales de Banorte no tienen potencial de mejora debido a que ya se ubican en el nivel más alto de la escala nacional;

OTRAS CALIFICACIONES DE DEUDA: FACTORES CLAVE DE CALIFICACIÓN

Deuda Sénior Quirografaria de Banorte: Las calificaciones de la deuda sénior quirografaria local están alineadas con la calificación nacional de largo plazo de Banorte de ‘AAA(mex)’, dado que la probabilidad de incumplimiento de las notas es la misma que la del emisor y se esperan recuperaciones promedio.

Banorte Clasificado como D-SIB: La GSR de Banorte de ‘bb+’ refleja su elevada importancia sistémica. El banco está definido como un banco de importancia sistémica local (D-SIB). Debido a su participación de mercado y amplia interconexión dentro del sistema financiero, Fitch considera elevada la propensión de las autoridades a proporcionar apoyo para evitar riesgos de contagio.

Al 2T26, la participación de mercado de Banorte en depósitos de clientes fue de 14%, lo que lo posiciona como el segundo banco del sistema. Sin embargo, Fitch considera que la probabilidad de apoyo para Banorte es menor que para otros bancos grandes vinculados a políticas públicas debido a la propiedad privada de Banorte.

OTRAS CALIFICACIONES DE DEUDA: SENSIBILIDAD DE CALIFICACIÓN

Calificaciones de Deuda

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación negativa/baja:

--una baja de la calificación de la deuda sénior de Banorte reflejaría cualquier baja en las calificaciones nacionales del emisor.

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación positiva/alza:

--la calificación de la deuda sénior de Banorte no tiene potencial de mejora debido a que es la más alta de la escala nacional.

Calificación de Soporte Gubernamental

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación negativa/baja:

--la GSR de Banorte podría bajar si la capacidad del soberano para brindar apoyo al banco se debilita como resultado de una baja de la calificación soberana, o si disminuye la propensión del soberano a proporcionar dicho apoyo.

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación positiva/alza:

-- un alza de la GSR de Banorte es posible en caso de un alza de la calificación soberana que coincida con un fortalecimiento de la capacidad y propensión del soberano para brindar apoyo al banco.

SUBSIDIARIAS Y AFILIADAS: FACTORES CLAVE DE CALIFICACIÓN

Calificaciones de GFNorte Igualadas con las de Banorte: Fitch considera que el riesgo de incumplimiento de GFNorte es sustancialmente el mismo que el de Banorte debido a la dependencia de GFNorte de los flujos de dividendos provenientes del banco y del valor de su inversión en este. Las calificaciones de GFNorte también reflejan, con alta relevancia, su bajo índice de doble apalancamiento, medido como inversiones en subsidiarias respecto del patrimonio tangible.

El índice de doble apalancamiento fue de 98.2% en el 2T26, frente a 96.4% en el 2T25, y se mantuvo muy por debajo del umbral de 120% de Fitch.

El Soporte Sustenta las Calificaciones Nacionales de las Subsidiarias: Las calificaciones nacionales de CB Banorte, AyF Banorte y Almacenadora Banorte reflejan el perfil crediticio de su compañía controladora, GFNorte, que a su vez está determinado por Banorte, la principal entidad operativa del grupo. Fitch incorpora el soporte explícito que se esperaría que el grupo financiero proporcionara a estas entidades, dados sus roles en la estrategia de diversificación de negocios del grupo y la obligación legal de GFNorte de respaldar a sus subsidiarias.

SUBSIDIARIAS Y AFILIADAS: SENSIBILIDAD DE CALIFICACIÓN

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación negativa/baja:

-las IDR de GFNorte podrían bajar si se produce un aumento significativo y sostenido del doble apalancamiento por encima de 120%. Esto daría lugar a calificaciones un nivel por debajo de las IDR de Banorte;

--cualquier movimiento negativo en las calificaciones de las subsidiarias no bancarias de GFNorte derivaría de una acción negativa sobre las calificaciones nacionales de Banorte;

--un cambio en la importancia estratégica para el grupo y el banco de las subsidiarias no bancarias de GFNorte podría afectar sus calificaciones.

Factores que podrían, individual o colectivamente, conducir a una acción de calificación positiva/alza:

--un alza de las IDR de GFNorte resultaría de cualquier cambio positivo en la VR de Banorte;

--las calificaciones de las subsidiarias no bancarias de GFNorte se encuentran en el nivel más alto de la escala nacional; por lo tanto, no existe posibilidad de un alza de estas calificaciones.

AJUSTES A LA CALIFICACIÓN VR

La puntuación del EO de ‘bb+’ se ubica por debajo de la puntuación implícita de la categoría ‘bbb’ debido al siguiente motivo de ajuste: desempeño económico (negativo).

La puntuación de calidad de activos de ‘bbb-’ se ubica por encima de la puntuación implícita de la categoría ‘bb’ debido al siguiente motivo de ajuste: garantías y reservas (positivo).

La puntuación de capitalización y apalancamiento de ‘bbb-’ se ubica por encima de la puntuación implícita de la categoría ‘bb’ debido al siguiente motivo de ajuste: apalancamiento y cálculo de riesgos (positivo).

La puntuación de fondeo y liquidez de ‘bbb-’ se ubica por encima de la puntuación implícita de la categoría ‘bb’ debido al siguiente motivo de ajuste: estructura de depósitos (positivo).

PARTICIPACIÓN

La(s) calificación(es) mencionada(s) fue(ron) requerida(s) y se asignó(aron) o se le(s) dio seguimiento por solicitud del (los) emisor(es) o entidad(es) calificada(s) o de un tercero relacionado. Cualquier excepción se indicará.

RESUMEN DE AJUSTES A LOS ESTADOS FINANCIEROS

El cálculo de capital tangible de Fitch excluyó las partidas del balance general de gastos pagados por anticipado y otros activos diferidos del capital contable.

Un puntaje de ‘3’ significa que los aspectos ESG son neutrales para el crédito o tienen un impacto crediticio mínimo en la entidad, ya sea debido a la naturaleza de los mismos o a la forma en que son gestionados por la entidad. Fitch Ratings-Monterrey-28 October 2026:

Fitch Ratings has affirmed the Long-Term Foreign and Local Currency Issuer Default Ratings (IDRs) of Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. de C.V. (GFNorte) and Banco Mercantil del Norte, S.A., Institucion de Banca Multiple, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Banorte) at 'BBB-' due to an affirmation of Banorte's Viability Rating (VR) at 'bbb-'. The Short-Term Foreign and Local Currency IDRs were affirmed at 'F3', and Banorte's Government Support Rating (GSR) was affirmed at 'bb+'. The Rating Outlook for the Long-Term IDRs is Positive.

Fitch has also affirmed the Long- and Short-Term National Scale Ratings of Banorte, Arrendadora y Factor Banorte, S.A. de C.V., SOFOM, E.R., Grupo Financiero Banorte (AyF Banorte), Casa de Bolsa Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Grupo Financiero Banorte (CB Banorte) and Almacenadora Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Organizacion Auxiliar del Credito, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Almacenadora Banorte) at 'AAA(mex)' and 'F1+(mex)', respectively. The Rating Outlook for all the Long-Term National Ratings is Stable. A full list of ratings actions is at the end of this press release.

Key Rating Drivers

Stable Operating Environment: The score for the operating environment (OE) was affirmed at 'bb+' with a stable outlook and is below its implied score of 'bbb'. Operating conditions for Mexican banks remain good, but subdued economic performance continues to influence banks' ability to generate businesses. The country's estimated GDP per capita for 2026 is USD16,234, and Fitch's Operational Risk Index (ORI) percentile was 45.8% in October 2026, supporting the implied OE score of 'bbb'. Fitch adjusted the implied OE score, viewing economic performance as a negative factor.

Positive Outlook: The Positive Rating Outlook reflects the continued improvements in Banorte's overall business and financial profiles. Fitch expects these improvements to be sustained, with an operating profit-to-risk weighted assets (RWA) ratios above 4.75% and a common equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio close to 14%, while reducing gradually its exposure to the public sector. If sustained, these improvements could lead to positive rating action over the next 12 months.

Strong Performance Drives Ratings: Banorte's IDRs and National Ratings are driven by its 'bbb-' VR. The VR reflects the bank's consolidated business profile and strong risk framework, as well as good financial performance over the economic cycle. Fitch affirmed Banorte's Business Profile score at 'bbb-' with outlook positive. Fitch believes Banorte will continue to consolidate its leading position in Mexico by gaining market share and widening the gap among its followers. Banorte's four-year average total operating income (TOI) from 2022-2025 was USD6.5 billion, gradually exceeding that of its closest peers.

Prudent Risk Management: Fitch affirmed Banorte's risk profile score at 'bbb-' with outlook positive. This reflects the bank's sound and consistent underwriting standards across economic cycles, as well as its solid risk-control framework, which Fitch views as aligned with its business profile. Strong capitalization metrics and ample collateral have consistently supported prudent balance-sheet growth. These factors mitigate Banorte's higher concentrations relative to certain peers. Banorte's consistent risk profile, along with a robust risk infrastructure, ensures effective credit quality control and monitoring of various risks. A sustained downward trend in the exposure to the Mexican sovereign would be viewed favorably by Fitch and could support upward momentum in the Risk Profile assessment.

Sound Asset Quality: Banorte's asset quality score of 'bbb-' reflects broadly stable metrics over the past five years. Stage 3 loans as a proportion of gross loans were 1.5% in 2Q26 from a four-year average of 1.1%, due to an isolated commercial loan exposure from 3Q25 and the consolidation of the loan portfolio of Tarjetas del Futuro. However, NPL metrics across all credit segments have been stable and compare favorably to peers. Fitch expects the NPL ratio to return to historical levels. Banorte's prudent underwriting standards and high collateral coverage continue to support the 'bbb-' asset quality score, which should support recovery prospects.

Strong and Resilient Profitability: Fitch's 'bbb-' assessment of Banorte's earnings and profitability reflects its consistent operating profitability, supported by resilient net interest income, moderate credit costs and operating efficiencies. The operating profit-to-RWA ratio was 6.2% in 2Q26, compared with 5.9% on average for 2022-2025. Banorte's profitability metrics compare favorable to peers, and it is one of the most profitable banks among Mexico's largest banks. Fitch expects core profitability metrics to be sustained close to 6%.

Strong Capitalization: Fitch assesses Banorte's capitalization and leverage score at 'bbb-', reflecting robust capital metrics and ample buffers above local regulatory requirements. The bank's CET1 ratio was 12.6% in 2Q26, down from 14% in 2Q25 due to dividend payments. Fitch expects the CET1 ratio to recover to 13% or above through the bank's earnings generation. Loss-absorbing hybrid instruments, primarily additional Tier 1 (AT1) securities, supported a total capital ratio of 21.5% on the same date, which Fitch views positively. Fitch expects Banorte's capital to remain sufficient to absorb expected loan growth and support consistent dividend distributions.

Enhanced Funding and Liquidity Profile: Banorte's funding and liquidity factor score of 'bbb-' reflects structural improvements in its funding mix and financing costs. The bank's loans-to-deposits ratio was 103.5% in 2Q26, compared with a 2022-2025 average of 102.0%. Its net stable funding ratio was 132% in 2Q26. Increasing demand for deposits is a key component of Banorte's funding strategy; these represented 67.4% of total customer deposits in 2Q26 and are trending toward peer levels.

Rating Sensitivities Factors that Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--The Outlook could be revised to Stable if Banorte is not able to sustain the improvements in its business and financial profiles.

--Banorte's VRs and IDRs are sensitive to a rating action on Mexico's sovereign ratings or a downward revision of Fitch's OE assessment.

--Banorte's ratings could be downgraded if financial performance deteriorates consistently, with the operating profit-to-RWA ratio falling below 2.5%, the CET1-to-RWA ratio decreasing below 12% or a weakening of Fitch's risk profile assessment, denoting asset quality deterioration.

--A significant increase in the bank's exposure to the sovereign may also trigger a VR downgrade to the same level of the sovereign rating.

--Banorte's national scale ratings will reflect any change in local relativities.

Factors that Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Positive Rating Action/Upgrade

--The VR and IDRs could be upgraded if the sovereign rating is upgraded and Fitch revises upward its OE assessment, while the bank maintains very strong business and financial profiles.

--Banorte's ratings could be upgraded if TOI growth continues, financial performance remains solid and consistent, an operating profit-to-RWA ratio above 4.75%, a CET1-to-RWA and total capital ratios close or above 14% and 21%, respectively, asset quality metrics remain at reasonable levels, and Mexican sovereign exposure declines, considering a sovereign debt to CET1 ratio at or below 2x.

--Banorte's national scale ratings cannot be upgraded because they are at the highest level on the national ratings scale.

OTHER DEBT AND ISSUER RATINGS: KEY RATING DRIVERS

Banorte's Senior Unsecured Debt: The local senior unsecured debt ratings are at the same level as Banorte's 'AAA(mex)' National Long-Term Rating, as the notes' likelihood of default is the same as that of the issuer and average expected recoveries.

Banorte Classified as D-SIB: Banorte's 'bb+' GSR reflects its high systemic importance. The bank is defined as a domestic systemically important bank (D-SIB). Fitch considers the authorities' propensity to support as high given its market share and ample interconnectivity within the financial system, to avoid contagion risks.

As of 2Q26, Banorte's market share in customer deposits was 14.0%, ranking as the second-largest bank in the system. However, Fitch believes the likelihood of support for Banorte is lower than other large policy banks due to Banorte's private ownership.

OTHER DEBT AND ISSUER RATINGS: RATING SENSITIVITIES

Debt Ratings

Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--A downgrade to Banorte's senior debt rating would mirror any downgrade in the issuer's national scale ratings.

Factors that could, individually or collectively, lead to positive rating action/upgrade:

--Banorte's senior debt rating has no improvement potential because it is at the highest level on the national rating scale.

Government Support Rating

Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--A downgrade to Banorte's GSR could occur if the sovereign's ability to support the bank is weakened by a sovereign rating downgrade, or if the sovereign's propensity to support the bank becomes less likely.

Factors that could, individually or collectively, lead to positive rating action/upgrade:

--An upgrade to Banorte's GSR is possible in the event of a sovereign upgrade coinciding with a strengthening of the sovereign's ability and propensity to support the bank.

SUBSIDIARIES & AFFILIATES: KEY RATING DRIVERS

GFNorte's Ratings Equalized with Banorte's: Fitch considers GFNorte's failure risk to be substantially the same as that of Banorte, given GFNorte's reliance on dividend flows from, and the value of, its investment in the bank. GFNorte's ratings also reflect its low double-leverage ratio, a highly relevant factor measured as investments in subsidiaries relative to tangible equity.

The double-leverage ratio was 98.2% at 2Q26, compared with 96.4% at 2Q25, and remained well below Fitch's 120% threshold.

Support Underpins Subsidiaries' National Ratings: The National Ratings of CB Banorte, AyF Banorte and Almacenadora Banorte reflect the credit profile of their holding company, GFNorte, which is driven by Banorte, the group's main operating entity. Fitch factors in the explicit support that the financial group would provide to these entities, given their roles in the group's business-diversification strategy and GFNorte's legal obligation to support its subsidiaries.

SUBSIDIARIES AND AFFILIATES: RATING SENSITIVITIES

FactorsThat Could, Individually or Collectively, Leadto Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--GFNorte's IDRs could be downgraded if there is a significant and sustained increase in double leverage above 120%. This would lead to one level below Banorte' IDRs.

--Any negative movement in the ratings of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries would be driven by a negative action on Banorte's national ratings.

--A change in the strategic importance of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries to the group and the bank could negatively affect their ratings.

FactorsThat Could, Individuallyor Collectively, Leadto Positive Rating Action/Upgrade

--An upgrade of GFNorte's IDRs would result from any positive change in Banorte's VR.

--The ratings of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries are at the highest level on the national scale; therefore, there is no possibility of an upgrade to these ratings.

VR ADJUSTMENTS

The operating environment score of 'bb+' is below the 'bbb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): economic performance (negative).

The asset quality score of 'bbb-' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): collateral and reserves (positive).

The capitalization & leverage score of 'bbb-' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): leverage and risk-weight calculation (positive).

The funding & liquidity score of 'bbb-' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): deposit structure (positive).

Summary of Financial Adjustments
