Fitch Ratings-Monterrey-28 October 2026:

Fitch Ratings has affirmed the Long-Term Foreign and Local Currency Issuer Default Ratings (IDRs) of Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. de C.V. (GFNorte) and Banco Mercantil del Norte, S.A., Institucion de Banca Multiple, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Banorte) at 'BBB-' due to an affirmation of Banorte's Viability Rating (VR) at 'bbb-'. The Short-Term Foreign and Local Currency IDRs were affirmed at 'F3', and Banorte's Government Support Rating (GSR) was affirmed at 'bb+'. The Rating Outlook for the Long-Term IDRs is Positive.

Fitch has also affirmed the Long- and Short-Term National Scale Ratings of Banorte, Arrendadora y Factor Banorte, S.A. de C.V., SOFOM, E.R., Grupo Financiero Banorte (AyF Banorte), Casa de Bolsa Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Grupo Financiero Banorte (CB Banorte) and Almacenadora Banorte, S.A. de C.V., Organizacion Auxiliar del Credito, Grupo Financiero Banorte (Almacenadora Banorte) at 'AAA(mex)' and 'F1+(mex)', respectively. The Rating Outlook for all the Long-Term National Ratings is Stable. A full list of ratings actions is at the end of this press release.

Key Rating Drivers

Stable Operating Environment: The score for the operating environment (OE) was affirmed at 'bb+' with a stable outlook and is below its implied score of 'bbb'. Operating conditions for Mexican banks remain good, but subdued economic performance continues to influence banks' ability to generate businesses. The country's estimated GDP per capita for 2026 is USD16,234, and Fitch's Operational Risk Index (ORI) percentile was 45.8% in October 2026, supporting the implied OE score of 'bbb'. Fitch adjusted the implied OE score, viewing economic performance as a negative factor.

Positive Outlook: The Positive Rating Outlook reflects the continued improvements in Banorte's overall business and financial profiles. Fitch expects these improvements to be sustained, with an operating profit-to-risk weighted assets (RWA) ratios above 4.75% and a common equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio close to 14%, while reducing gradually its exposure to the public sector. If sustained, these improvements could lead to positive rating action over the next 12 months.

Strong Performance Drives Ratings: Banorte's IDRs and National Ratings are driven by its 'bbb-' VR. The VR reflects the bank's consolidated business profile and strong risk framework, as well as good financial performance over the economic cycle. Fitch affirmed Banorte's Business Profile score at 'bbb-' with outlook positive. Fitch believes Banorte will continue to consolidate its leading position in Mexico by gaining market share and widening the gap among its followers. Banorte's four-year average total operating income (TOI) from 2022-2025 was USD6.5 billion, gradually exceeding that of its closest peers.

Prudent Risk Management: Fitch affirmed Banorte's risk profile score at 'bbb-' with outlook positive. This reflects the bank's sound and consistent underwriting standards across economic cycles, as well as its solid risk-control framework, which Fitch views as aligned with its business profile. Strong capitalization metrics and ample collateral have consistently supported prudent balance-sheet growth. These factors mitigate Banorte's higher concentrations relative to certain peers. Banorte's consistent risk profile, along with a robust risk infrastructure, ensures effective credit quality control and monitoring of various risks. A sustained downward trend in the exposure to the Mexican sovereign would be viewed favorably by Fitch and could support upward momentum in the Risk Profile assessment.

Sound Asset Quality: Banorte's asset quality score of 'bbb-' reflects broadly stable metrics over the past five years. Stage 3 loans as a proportion of gross loans were 1.5% in 2Q26 from a four-year average of 1.1%, due to an isolated commercial loan exposure from 3Q25 and the consolidation of the loan portfolio of Tarjetas del Futuro. However, NPL metrics across all credit segments have been stable and compare favorably to peers. Fitch expects the NPL ratio to return to historical levels. Banorte's prudent underwriting standards and high collateral coverage continue to support the 'bbb-' asset quality score, which should support recovery prospects.

Strong and Resilient Profitability: Fitch's 'bbb-' assessment of Banorte's earnings and profitability reflects its consistent operating profitability, supported by resilient net interest income, moderate credit costs and operating efficiencies. The operating profit-to-RWA ratio was 6.2% in 2Q26, compared with 5.9% on average for 2022-2025. Banorte's profitability metrics compare favorable to peers, and it is one of the most profitable banks among Mexico's largest banks. Fitch expects core profitability metrics to be sustained close to 6%.

Strong Capitalization: Fitch assesses Banorte's capitalization and leverage score at 'bbb-', reflecting robust capital metrics and ample buffers above local regulatory requirements. The bank's CET1 ratio was 12.6% in 2Q26, down from 14% in 2Q25 due to dividend payments. Fitch expects the CET1 ratio to recover to 13% or above through the bank's earnings generation. Loss-absorbing hybrid instruments, primarily additional Tier 1 (AT1) securities, supported a total capital ratio of 21.5% on the same date, which Fitch views positively. Fitch expects Banorte's capital to remain sufficient to absorb expected loan growth and support consistent dividend distributions.

Enhanced Funding and Liquidity Profile: Banorte's funding and liquidity factor score of 'bbb-' reflects structural improvements in its funding mix and financing costs. The bank's loans-to-deposits ratio was 103.5% in 2Q26, compared with a 2022-2025 average of 102.0%. Its net stable funding ratio was 132% in 2Q26. Increasing demand for deposits is a key component of Banorte's funding strategy; these represented 67.4% of total customer deposits in 2Q26 and are trending toward peer levels.

Rating Sensitivities Factors that Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--The Outlook could be revised to Stable if Banorte is not able to sustain the improvements in its business and financial profiles.

--Banorte's VRs and IDRs are sensitive to a rating action on Mexico's sovereign ratings or a downward revision of Fitch's OE assessment.

--Banorte's ratings could be downgraded if financial performance deteriorates consistently, with the operating profit-to-RWA ratio falling below 2.5%, the CET1-to-RWA ratio decreasing below 12% or a weakening of Fitch's risk profile assessment, denoting asset quality deterioration.

--A significant increase in the bank's exposure to the sovereign may also trigger a VR downgrade to the same level of the sovereign rating.

--Banorte's national scale ratings will reflect any change in local relativities.

Factors that Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Positive Rating Action/Upgrade

--The VR and IDRs could be upgraded if the sovereign rating is upgraded and Fitch revises upward its OE assessment, while the bank maintains very strong business and financial profiles.

--Banorte's ratings could be upgraded if TOI growth continues, financial performance remains solid and consistent, an operating profit-to-RWA ratio above 4.75%, a CET1-to-RWA and total capital ratios close or above 14% and 21%, respectively, asset quality metrics remain at reasonable levels, and Mexican sovereign exposure declines, considering a sovereign debt to CET1 ratio at or below 2x.

--Banorte's national scale ratings cannot be upgraded because they are at the highest level on the national ratings scale.

OTHER DEBT AND ISSUER RATINGS: KEY RATING DRIVERS

Banorte's Senior Unsecured Debt: The local senior unsecured debt ratings are at the same level as Banorte's 'AAA(mex)' National Long-Term Rating, as the notes' likelihood of default is the same as that of the issuer and average expected recoveries.

Banorte Classified as D-SIB: Banorte's 'bb+' GSR reflects its high systemic importance. The bank is defined as a domestic systemically important bank (D-SIB). Fitch considers the authorities' propensity to support as high given its market share and ample interconnectivity within the financial system, to avoid contagion risks.

As of 2Q26, Banorte's market share in customer deposits was 14.0%, ranking as the second-largest bank in the system. However, Fitch believes the likelihood of support for Banorte is lower than other large policy banks due to Banorte's private ownership.

OTHER DEBT AND ISSUER RATINGS: RATING SENSITIVITIES

Debt Ratings

Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--A downgrade to Banorte's senior debt rating would mirror any downgrade in the issuer's national scale ratings.

Factors that could, individually or collectively, lead to positive rating action/upgrade:

--Banorte's senior debt rating has no improvement potential because it is at the highest level on the national rating scale.

Government Support Rating

Factors That Could, Individually or Collectively, Lead to Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--A downgrade to Banorte's GSR could occur if the sovereign's ability to support the bank is weakened by a sovereign rating downgrade, or if the sovereign's propensity to support the bank becomes less likely.

Factors that could, individually or collectively, lead to positive rating action/upgrade:

--An upgrade to Banorte's GSR is possible in the event of a sovereign upgrade coinciding with a strengthening of the sovereign's ability and propensity to support the bank.

SUBSIDIARIES & AFFILIATES: KEY RATING DRIVERS

GFNorte's Ratings Equalized with Banorte's: Fitch considers GFNorte's failure risk to be substantially the same as that of Banorte, given GFNorte's reliance on dividend flows from, and the value of, its investment in the bank. GFNorte's ratings also reflect its low double-leverage ratio, a highly relevant factor measured as investments in subsidiaries relative to tangible equity.

The double-leverage ratio was 98.2% at 2Q26, compared with 96.4% at 2Q25, and remained well below Fitch's 120% threshold.

Support Underpins Subsidiaries' National Ratings: The National Ratings of CB Banorte, AyF Banorte and Almacenadora Banorte reflect the credit profile of their holding company, GFNorte, which is driven by Banorte, the group's main operating entity. Fitch factors in the explicit support that the financial group would provide to these entities, given their roles in the group's business-diversification strategy and GFNorte's legal obligation to support its subsidiaries.

SUBSIDIARIES AND AFFILIATES: RATING SENSITIVITIES

FactorsThat Could, Individually or Collectively, Leadto Negative Rating Action/Downgrade

--GFNorte's IDRs could be downgraded if there is a significant and sustained increase in double leverage above 120%. This would lead to one level below Banorte' IDRs.

--Any negative movement in the ratings of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries would be driven by a negative action on Banorte's national ratings.

--A change in the strategic importance of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries to the group and the bank could negatively affect their ratings.

FactorsThat Could, Individuallyor Collectively, Leadto Positive Rating Action/Upgrade

--An upgrade of GFNorte's IDRs would result from any positive change in Banorte's VR.

--The ratings of GFNorte's nonbank subsidiaries are at the highest level on the national scale; therefore, there is no possibility of an upgrade to these ratings.

VR ADJUSTMENTS

The operating environment score of 'bb+' is below the 'bbb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): economic performance (negative).

The asset quality score of 'bbb-' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): collateral and reserves (positive).

The capitalization & leverage score of 'bbb-' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): leverage and risk-weight calculation (positive).

The funding & liquidity score of 'bbb-' is above the 'bb' category implied score due to the following adjustment reason(s): deposit structure (positive).

Summary of Financial Adjustments

Fitch's tangible capital calculation excluded prepaid expenses and other deferred assets from shareholders' equity.

GFNorte's IDRs and Almacenadora Banorte, AyF Banorte, Casa de Bolsa Banorte's ratings and Outlook are linked with those of Banorte.

ESG Considerations

The highest level of ESG credit relevance is a score of '3', unless otherwise disclosed in this section. A score of '3' means ESG issues are credit-neutral or have only a minimal credit impact on the entity, either due to their nature or the way in which they are being managed by the entity. Fitch's ESG Relevance Scores are not inputs in the rating process; they are an observation on the relevance and materiality of ESG factors in the rating decision. Changes headline, adds election recognition in paragraph 5, comment from electoral authority chief in paragraph 6

  • Bolsonaro loses to Lula by around 4.5 million votes
  • Bolsonaro defied a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports
  • Analysts say Bolsonaro's request to annul election result faces little chance of success

By Fernando Cardoso and Luciana Magalhaes

SAO PAULO, Oct 28 (Reuters) - Senator Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself Brazil's rightful leader on Wednesday after arriving in the United States, alleging he was the victim of an electoral coup by the country's Supreme Court and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who won the vote by over 4 million votes.

Bolsonaro arrived in Miami after leaving Brazil, where he refused to comply with a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports. He thanked Argentine leader Javier Milei for helping him make the journey and US President Donald Trump, who granted him and his family entry visas, for welcoming him.

In an initial open letter posted on X, Bolsonaro declared himself "the elected president." He then deleted that version and updated it with another letter in which he said he was the rightful "leader" of Brazil.

"I want to say, not only to my 60 million voters but to the Brazilian people, that I am the leader and that the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny," he said in the updated version.

Lula's victory has been recognized by Brazil's federal electoral court, global leaders, international observers, and Bolsonaro's own party.

Brazil's election took place in full compliance with legal and constitutional requirements, electoral authority chief Kassio Nunes Marques said in a statement, without referencing Bolsonaro's letter.

Asked by reporters at Joint Base Andrews about Bolsonaro's comments, Trump declined to comment, reiterating earlier views that it was "a very strange election."

PROBLEM FOR WASHINGTON

Bolsonaro's declaration poses a problem for Washington as it seeks to navigate a rift with Latin America's largest country, home to the world's second-largest reserves of rare earths.

Lula has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaro family to help return them to power. Ahead of Sunday's election, Reuters reported on a US State Department campaign to restore the Bolsonaros to office. Washington denies meddling in Brazil's domestic affairs.

Trump has previously alleged Flavio's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution.

Jair Bolsonaro travelled to the United States after refusing to concede defeat to Lula in 2022. He eventually returned to Brazil but was sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup after supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia.

There was no immediate response from the State Department.

Neither Lula's office nor the Supreme Court immediately responded to requests for comment.

Lula, who served time on corruption convictions that were later annulled, said this week it was "shameful" Bolsonaro had not stayed in Brazil to prove his innocence.

NO PROOF

Bolsonaro left Brazil in secret after the Supreme Court issued the order, which relates to a money-laundering investigation in which he denies wrongdoing.

Bolsonaro, who had been widely expected to win Sunday's election, did not provide evidence for the alleged electoral fraud.

He based his rejection of the result on the fact that a Lula-appointed Supreme Court justice had extended voting by two hours on Sunday due to Lula campaign allegations of voter suppression in left-leaning northeastern states. However, Bolsonaro's campaign also sought an extension due to rain in conservative southern states.

Bolsonaro lost to Lula by around 4.5 million votes. Fewer than 35,000 votes, or some 0.03% of the total, were cast in the extra two hours of voting ordered by the Supreme Court, according to an analysis by Insper professor Pedro Burgos.

Analysts say Bolsonaro's request to annul the election result faces little chance of success.

In his letter, Bolsonaro denied fleeing Brazil, saying he left to protect himself and his family, and to avoid being the victim of a witch hunt he accused Lula and the Brazilian Supreme Court of carrying out.

"I want to make this clear: I did not flee Brazil," he said. "I left Brazil, but I did not abandon the Brazilian people."

(Reporting by Fernando Cardoso, Luciana Magalhaes, Gabriel Stargardter, Additional reporting by Alexandra Valencia in Quito, Gabriel Araujo in Sao Paulo, Maximilian Heath in Buenos Aires, Eva Marie Uzcategui in Miami and David Brunnstrom in Washington and Oliver Griffin in Sao Paulo
Editing by Ros Russell, Franklin Paul, Aurora Ellis, Rod Nickel)

(( Gabriel.Stargardter@thomsonreuters.com ; +55 21998116099; Reuters Messaging: gabriel.stargardter.thomsonreuters.com@reuters.net /))

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte (OMA) reported its operational and financial results for the third quarter of 2026, where the consolidated net profit of the airport group was 1.555 billion pesos, representing a 3% increase compared to the same quarter of the previous year.

Passenger traffic increased by 1.3% compared to the same period last year, totaling 7.7 million passengers.

The passenger mix for the quarter was 85.8% domestic and 14.2% international.

Domestic passenger traffic rose by 0.6% compared to the previous year, while international passenger traffic increased by 6%.

States with Highest and Lowest Passenger Traffic

The airports with the highest traffic growth were San Luis Potosí, which saw a 27.3% increase on routes to Mexico City (AIFA), Monterrey, Puerto Vallarta, Guadalajara, and Chicago.

Durango recorded a 32.3% increase on routes to Monterrey and Guadalajara; and Chihuahua had a 4.5% growth on routes to Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Torreón.

The sum of aeronautical and non-aeronautical revenues grew by 8.3% compared to the third quarter of 2025.

On the other hand, the airports with the largest decline in passenger volume, compared to the third quarter of 2025, were: Monterrey, down by 2.1%, primarily on routes to Toluca, Puerto Vallarta, and Ciudad Juárez.

Ciudad Juárez experienced a 5.1% decrease on routes to Monterrey and Mazatlán.

OMA's cargo operations grew by 42.4% in terms of revenue compared to the third quarter of 2025, mainly due to new clients in Monterrey and the handling of additional high-value cargo operations along with longer storage times for merchandise in our warehouses.

Aeronautical revenues increased by 6.7%, driven by a 7.4% rise in national TUA revenue.

International TUA revenue rose by 4% due to a 6% increase in international traffic during the quarter, partially offset by the appreciation of the peso against the U.S. dollar, while non-aeronautical revenues grew by 13.3%.

The fastest-growing sectors were: VIP lounges, which increased by 28% due to greater penetration and the opening of a new VIP lounge at Torreón airport.

Restaurants saw a 13.5% rise, boosted by an increase in passengers and the opening of new units at the airports in Durango and Torreón.

Parking facilities grew by 6.7%, driven by increased average rates at the airports in Monterrey, Chihuahua, and Ciudad Juárez.

Retail stores grew by 18.5%, due to the opening of new units at the airports in Monterrey, Culiacán, and Zihuatanejo.

Aeroméxico resumes flights from Mexico City to Saltillo, Coahuila; the route will operate starting in 2027.

Cozumel will have its first direct flight from Europe; the Milan-Cozumel route will begin on December 24.

More flights, less market: the Mexican sky faces its test.

BUENOS AIRES, 28 oct (Reuters) - Argentina adjudicó títulos del Tesoro por un valor efectivo de 11,56 billones de pesos (unos 7.497 millones de dólares) en una licitación doméstica de varios instrumentos para refinanciar vencimientos, informó el miércoles la Secretaría de Finanzas.

La licitación, por la que se recibió un total de ofertas por 25,79 billones de pesos, abarcó una renovación ('rollover') del 107% de los vencimientos previstos.

El Tesoro buscó renovar originalmente unos 10,9 billones de pesos en vencimientos de deuda interna.

En esta ocasión, el menú volvió a ser relativamente corto en plazo amortizable, ofreciéndose una nueva 'Lecap' a febrero venidero, dos 'Boncer' (TZXM7 y TZXO7), el título 'Bontam' (TMG27), el dual CER/Tamar (TXMD8) y otro 'dollar linked' (D15E7).

"El resultado le permitió cumplir holgadamente con su programa de refinanciación sin tensionar la liquidez del sistema ni recurrir a sus depósitos en el Banco Central", dijo Eric Ritondale, economista jefe de Puente.

"La estrategia oficial volvió a apoyarse en extender vencimientos hacia el próximo mandato presidencial, aunque convalidando la preferencia de los inversores por plazos más cortos e instrumentos de cobertura indexada", agregó.

(1 dólar = 1.542 pesos ARS=RASL)

(Reporte de Jorge Otaola;
Editado por Eliana Raszewski)

A survey by Banco Provincia on over 320,000 private sector salary accounts concluded that 36% of workers run out of their monthly salary by the 10th of the month .

The provincial financial institution noted that income "runs out faster" due to fixed expenses and credit card payments, in a context of widespread declining consumption.

The analysis, conducted in July 2026, focused on employees who receive their salaries through the institution and do not transfer them to other banks. "The study considers a person to have run out of salary funds when the balance from that income reaches zero due to payments, expenditures, withdrawals, transfers, or purchases of dollars," it clarified.

In this context, it was found that within the first five days following payment, the entire analyzed group had already used half of their remuneration. "In those first days of the month, automatic debits come in, and credit cards along with a large portion of fixed expenses, such as rent, are paid," the document observed.

By the 10th, 36% of the account holders analyzed had run out of their salary funds. Meanwhile, by the 20th, this percentage rose to 57%. Thus, nearly six out of ten individuals no longer had money from their monthly earnings.

The survey noted that " salary runs out faster, but not because individuals are consuming more ." According to the institution's data, there was a 4.3% decline in real wages between July 2025 and July 2026, while real consumption made via credit cards and Cuenta DNI fell by 8.6% over the same period. "If we compare it to 2023, the drop in real consumption reaches 20%," it added.

This information becomes relevant after those who question the notion that some people struggle to make ends meet: " If they truly run out of money by the 20th, how do they live for 10 days without eating or drinking? Do you realize that this statement sounds nice, but it's as absurd as a house? Let's reflect. Let's not be manipulated by the bastards who have ruined the country."

"The report reflects how the loss of purchasing power in daily life impacts economic activity. Thus, considering that the macroeconomy is functioning when wages fall and families face greater difficulties to make ends meet is a very reductionist view of the economic reality in Argentina," stated Juan Cuattromo, president of Banco Provincia.

The analysis detected a trend between December 2023 and 2025 . During this period, the proportion of workers who ran out of salary before the 10th increased from 17.9% to 23.2%. The share of income already utilized by the day after payment also rose: from 18.5% to 23.5%.

The Most Affected

Banco Provincia's survey emphasized that those on lower incomes are the most affected: 56% ran out of salary funds before the 10th, and half depleted their resources by the 7th . In the lower middle-income segments, the percentage was 40%, with half running out of funds by the 14th.

" As income levels increase, the situation improves, although it still shows signs of deterioration : among the high-income sectors, 21% ran out of salary before the 10th, and half arrived at the 24th without funds," the study detailed.

Historical comparisons also show that the worsening was more pronounced in lower-income segments, even when contrasting individuals with similar purchasing power. Among those earning the equivalent of $1.2 million per month, the proportion of workers who ran out of money before the 10th increased by 5.9 percentage points between December 2023 and December 2025. For incomes of $2 million, the rise was 5.2 points, while for salaries equivalent to $4 million, the increase was 1.5 points.

For much of the year, the evolution of the Brazilian real helped cushion Argentina's loss of exchange rate competitiveness . However, after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva surprised everyone at the polls on Sunday and won the elections in Brazil, the currency of the neighboring country depreciated by nearly 8% within the week, putting pressure back on the Argentine real exchange rate.

The strong adverse reaction from Brazilian markets has raised some alarm over the impact that a depreciation of the currency of Argentina's main trading partner could have on the local economy. In September, Argentina exported US$1.206 billion to Brazil and imported goods worth US$1.375 billion, according to the latest report from the Argentine Trade Exchange (ICA) prepared by Indec.

Molinos acquires Ayudín and accelerates its expansion beyond food

"The devaluation of the real makes it more expensive for Brazilians to buy Argentine products, as the peso does not fully accompany the depreciation of the Brazilian currency. This is a factor that could negatively affect the volume of exports from Argentina to Brazil. Additionally, there is a risk that a fiscal adjustment in the neighboring country could lead to a decline in economic activity, reducing demand for Argentine products," analyzed Andrés Reschini, head of F2 Finanzas.

However, Reschini deemed it premature to quantify those risks, stating that, for now, he does not observe significant concern in the market. In his view, part of the correction in Brazilian financial assets reflects a realignment of expectations prior to the elections, rather than a conclusive signal about what will happen in the coming years.

"A positive for Argentina is that the real, after the shock it experienced on Monday following the elections, has stabilized at levels around 5.30 per dollar. It was not as drastic as it seemed on Monday, and some correction occurred. Nonetheless, it is true that the Brazilian currency had been an ally of the Argentine real exchange rate throughout the year. It was practically the only currency against which Argentina could maintain its competitiveness, as the real had been appreciating. In fact, it is still at lower levels than at the end of last year," noted Martín Polo, an economist and founder of Polomics.

With the recent movement, the Argentine multilateral real exchange rate is estimated to have fallen by about 1.5% this month. Moreover, when analyzing the exchange rate from a historical perspective, there is a decline of nearly 12% for the year to date, bringing the real exchange rate to its lowest level since mid-last year.

Surge in ticket sales to Brazil due to the fall of the real

"If the real depreciates, everything we import from Brazil becomes cheaper, and everything we export to them becomes more expensive. In a context where the government has opened imports significantly as one of the tools to contain internal prices, this puts local producers who compete against Brazilian products in a more difficult position, as they gain an exchange rate advantage, a competitive edge that Argentina lacks and, as seems evident, will not have in the short term," stated financial analyst Christian Buteler.

For the economist, the government continues to use the exchange rate as a tool to control inflation. In that sense, he observed that despite the increased demand for dollars on Monday following the election reactions in Brazil, the Central Bank did not purchase foreign currency, and the Treasury even sold. The following day, when the exchange rate dropped slightly, the monetary authority also did not intervene with purchases. Today, for the third consecutive session, there was a repeat of zero interventions. This situation contrasts with the reserves purchasing dynamic maintained by the Central Bank throughout most of the year.

"The government does not want the exchange rate to rise, although it advanced by 0.75% the previous day, a reaction that was not too severe. In this context, a weaker real complicates matters, and while it affects tourism and makes vacations in Brazil cheaper, it also complicates the situation for Argentine companies. Nonetheless, what we observed in the early days of this week was a market reaction because the result was contrary to expectations. It was believed that Flávio Bolsonaro would win, but that did not happen. However, the evolution of the real, the stock market, and bonds will depend on how the Brazilian economy performs and the international context over the next four years," added Buteler.

Looking ahead, Polo indicated that the main variable to follow is the level of activity in Brazil, the primary destination for Argentine exports, especially industrial ones. He explained that it is more favorable for Argentina if the Brazilian economy grows at a high rate, even if that occurs with a more depreciated real, compared to a scenario of lower growth with a stronger currency. "The more Brazil grows, the more demand we will have, and vice versa," he concluded.

By Melisa ReinholdBrazilElections in BrazilMarketsInflation and pricesAccording to

lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261028:nNRA2h.html_limpio:
The Senate has authorized President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo to permit the entry of 28 members of the U.S. Navy SEALs Team 4 to Mexico for training during Event No. SOF 19 "Land and Maritime Operations Training with SEAL personnel and UNOPES."

This event is scheduled to take place from tomorrow, October 29, until April 15, 2027, at the facilities of the Advanced Training Center of the Mexican Navy, located in Donato Guerra, State of Mexico, and at the Naval Sector of Puerto Cortés, Isla Margarita, Baja California Sur.

The 28 U.S. military personnel will train 87 Mexican sailors from the Naval Special Operations Unit and the Naval Intelligence Unit, comprising 31 from the Special Forces Group, 20 from the Parachutist Rifle Battalion, 24 from the Amphibious Command Battalion, and 12 from the Naval Intelligence Unit.

The instructors from Navy SEAL Team 4 will enter national territory aboard a U.S. Air Force "Hercules C-130" aircraft equipped with tactical gear, ammunition, and organic weaponry, which is set to land on October 29, 2026, at La Paz Naval Air Base, Baja California Sur.

Members of the Naval Special Operations Unit of the Mexican Navy will receive and transport Team 4 of the Navy SEALs from the Naval Air Base to the Naval Sector of Puerto Cortés in Isla Margarita, Baja California Sur, and to the Advanced Training Center of the Mexican Navy in Donato Guerra, State of Mexico.

The U.S. military personnel will depart national territory aboard a "Hercules C-130" aircraft on April 15, 2027, from La Paz Naval Air Base, Baja California Sur.

According to the presidential request submitted to the upper house, the 2025-2030 Sectoral Marine Program aims to enhance the operational, technological, and strategic capabilities of the Mexican Navy to safeguard the population, protect national maritime interests, and ensure national security in Mexican marine areas, the continental shelf, insular territories, and strategic spaces.

It also includes Strategy 1.5, which aims to strengthen cooperation with allied countries' armed forces and international organizations to facilitate information exchange, joint training, and operational coordination on issues relating to national security, maritime interdiction, and combating transnational threats.

As part of the mechanism known as the Bilateral Military Cooperation Roundtable, the Secretary of the Navy (Semar) received an invitation from the government of the United States of America to participate in the aforementioned event, whose overall goal is to improve the capabilities of Mexico's Special Forces, enhance operational compatibility, and promote comprehensive programs that increase skills and operational capabilities focusing on close-quarters combat, contact reaction procedures, tactical medicine, urban patrolling, breaching/exploration, and explosive detection, sniper techniques, vessel boarding and hooking, and maritime interdiction operations.

MEXICO CITY, Oct 28 (Reuters) - Mexican Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard criticized US trade restrictions on Mexican farm exports on Wednesday, saying duties on products such as tomatoes and strawberries hurt consumers, fail to protect US growers and risk triggering a broader agricultural trade fight.

His warning comes at a sensitive moment in US-Mexico trade relations, with both governments still assessing whether they can clinch a broader deal to ease US tariffs on key Mexican industries before US midterm elections next week.

  • Speaking to journalists after an event in Mexico City, Ebrard said it was a "bad idea" to impose anti-dumping duties or other curbs on farm trade between the two countries, which are deeply integrated under a trilateral trade agreement with Canada

  • Ebrard cited the US duty on Mexican tomatoes as an example, which cut Mexican exports but caused Canadian and Guatemalan shipments to grow instead of boosting sales for Florida producers

  • The minister added a new US case involving Mexican strawberries would likely follow the same pattern, raising prices for US consumers

  • Mexico already has anti-dumping investigations into US pork and chicken, and if both sides continue, Ebrard said they could end up imposing more duties on each other

  • Mexico is also seeking relief from US tariffs on autos, steel and aluminum

  • Asked whether the US elections could alter the outlook, Ebrard declined to speculate, saying Mexico would keep arguing that using duties to reshape bilateral farm trade was a mistake

(Reporting by Kylie Madry, Editing by Natalia Siniawski)

(( Kylie.Madry@thomsonreuters.com ;))

The Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) starts the day in negative territory, while Wall Street indices trade mixed, influenced by expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will keep its interest rate unchanged.

The Price and Quotations Index (IPC) begins this Wednesday with a 0.52% drop, reaching 69,346.03 points (Mexico City, 8:12 AM), according to data from the exchange itself.

Meanwhile, Wall Street indices are trading mixed:

  • S&P 500 rises 0.23%, to 7,740.23 units
  • Nasdaq Composite decreases 0.10%, to 26,451.78 units
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average climbs 0.05%, to 52,405.47 points

BMV declines due to quarterly report season

The national stock market opens under pressure from the quarterly reporting season, as investors await the Federal Reserve's monetary policy announcement.

This Wednesday, Walmart de México y Centroamérica shares are the worst performers within the IPC, dropping 2.85% to 47.46 pesos. The retailer released its third-quarter financial results, reporting revenues of 248.828 billion pesos, a 3% increase compared to the same period last year.

The company reported a net profit of only 11.027 billion pesos, representing a drop of 6.1% compared to the third quarter of 2025.

In contrast, Inbursa shares are performing best within the BMV's main index, rising 0.65% to 46.27 pesos.

Wall Street trades mixed ahead of the Fed

This Wednesday, New York stock markets will be influenced by the Federal Reserve's monetary policy announcement, where officials are expected to keep the interest rate unchanged, in the range of 3.75% to 4%.

In addition to this announcement, investors will focus on the press conference of Kevin Warsh, Chairman of the United States central bank, where he could suggest further increases in rates due to global inflationary pressures.

In corporate news, SK hynix shares surged 11.14% to $161.64, after reporting quarterly revenues of 104.62 trillion won, exceeding the 78.85 trillion won that investors expected.

This represented a 327.9% increase compared to what was earned during the July-September 2025 period. Compared to the previous quarter, revenues rose by 31.9%.

It is expected that after the market closes, Microsoft and Alphabet, which are part of the 'Magnificent Seven' group, will release their quarterly results, potentially impacting artificial intelligence stocks.

Currently, Google's parent company's shares have risen 1.31% to $324.77, while Microsoft's shares decreased 0.46% to $528.90, according to Investing data.

Oil prices on October 28, 2026

Oil prices are starting the session higher after Houthi forces from Yemen, allied with Iran, intensified their attacks on energy facilities in Saudi Arabia, one of the main crude producers in the Middle East.

The December contract for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 1.90% to $101.80 per barrel. Meanwhile, the December contract for North Sea Brent increased 1.28% to $115.34, according to data from the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

The Houthis announced on Tuesday that they had targeted Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery with a missile. So far, Saudi authorities have not confirmed the attack on the facility, which has the capacity to produce 550,000 barrels per day.

Por Froilan Romero

SANTIAGO, 28 oct (Reuters) - Las principales monedas de América Latina registraron leves variaciones el miércoles, después de que la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos mantuviera sin cambios las tasas de interés.

* Tal como esperaba el mercado, la Fed optó por aplazar cualquier modificación de los costos de endeudamiento hasta después de las elecciones legislativas de Estados Unidos de la próxima semana y de que disponga de más datos sobre la evolución de la inflación.

* El presidente de la entidad, Kevin Warsh, dijo que las consideraciones políticas no influyeron en la decisión del banco central de mantener las tasas.

* El peso mexicano MXN= cotizaba cerca del cierre 18,6165 unidades por dólar, con un alza del 0,25%. El principal índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC .MXX, que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, caía un 0,73%, a 69.202,72 unidades, mientras los inversionistas seguían atentos a la publicación de resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre.

* El real brasileño BRL= se apreció un 0,04% a 5,3466 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice Bovespa .BVSP de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo retrocedió un 2,71%, a 170.946,55 puntos, tras un continuo ajuste luego de las elecciones presidenciales.

* El peso mayorista argentino ARS=RASL finalizó con una depreciación de 0,23% a 1.542 por dólar. La bolsa de Buenos Aires retrocedió un 1,17%, extendiendo las bajas de las dos jornadas anteriores.

* El peso chileno CLP=CL, CLP= cayó un 0,27%, a 984,50/984,80 unidades por dólar, luego de que el Banco Central mantuviera la tasa de interés en un 4,5%, como se esperaba, pero dejara abierta la puerta a una futura alza en medio de la persistencia inflacionaria.

* En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA .SPIPSA, bajó un 0,82%, a 10.677,94 puntos.

* El peso colombiano COP=RR terminó con caída de medio punto porcentual a 3.163,05 unidades por dólar, en su segunda baja consecutiva. En el mercado accionario, en tanto, el índice COLCAP .COLCAP finalizó con un retroceso del 0,03% a 2.505,83 puntos.

* La moneda peruana, el sol PEN=PDSB, se depreció un 0,06% a 3,4520/3,4530 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima .MXNUAMPESCPGPE retrocedía un 0,08% a 1.526,92 puntos.

(Reporte de Froilán Romero. Reporte adicional de Nelson Bocanegra en Bogotá, Noé Torres, en Ciudad de México, Hernán Nessi y Jorge Otaola en Buenos Aires; Editado por Manuel Farías y Javier Leira)

(( froilan.romero@thomsonreuters.com ; Mesa de Edición en Español; santiago.desk@thomsonreuters.com ))

Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta Company Profile

Corporación Inmobiliaria Vesta, SAB. de C.V., commonly known as Vesta, is a Mexican industrial real estate company focused on the development, acquisition, ownership, leasing and management of industrial properties. Its portfolio is designed to support manufacturing, logistics, distribution and other business operations.

Vesta provides industrial buildings, build-to-suit facilities and logistics-oriented properties for domestic and international companies. The company's properties are located in major industrial markets across Mexico, including regions serving automotive, aerospace, electronics, logistics and other manufacturing activities.

Vesta was established in Mexico in 1998 and has expanded its platform alongside the country's manufacturing and nearshoring industries.

• Wal-Mart de México declines after results
  • Brazilian stocks, real under pressure again
  • Chile holds interest rates at 4.5%, as expected

Updates with afternoon trading

By Sudeshna Ghoshal

Oct 28 (Reuters) - Most Latin American currencies slipped on Wednesday as traders parsed the US Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady, while attention shifted to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's choice for his cabinet in Brazil.

The Brazilian real BRL= weakened 0.1% against the US dollar, after a bruising selloff on Monday, when it marked its biggest one-day fall since 1999.

Brazil's benchmark index .BVSP was down 2.6%. Santander Brasil SANB3.SA declined 5.6% after a 15% drop in net profit in its Brazil market. Banco Bradesco BBDC4.SA and Itau Unibanco ITUB4.SA lost 6% and 3.1% respectively.

MSCI's index tracking regional currencies .MILA00000CUS was down 0.1%, while the stocks equivalent .MILA00000PUS was down 1.7%.

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's surprise reelection to a historic fourth term jolted markets that were pricing in a victory for right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, hoping for consolidation of public finances.

Lula is under pressure to pick a finance minister who can send a signal of fiscal discipline and reassure markets, with sources pointing to Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and Rafael Fonteles, the reelected governor of Piauí state.

ISRAEL ELECTION

On the election front, Israel also remained in focus. Its shekel ILS= weakened 2% after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won the support of an unexpectedly clear majority of Israeli Jews, apparently ensuring he will survive as prime minister, at least in a caretaker role.

Local shares .TA125 were down 2.5%.

"Israel is set for another round of protracted negotiations or a number of elections to break the deadlock," said Hasnain Malik, managing director, geopolitical risk and emerging markets equity strategy at Tellimer Research.

"The economic impact is likely minimal but the danger is increasing fissures in society, demonstrated by higher than expected votes for Likud, on the one hand, and the Arab parties, on the other."

FED IN FOCUS

On Wednesday, the US Federal Reserve also held interest rates steady, as expected.

The Colombian peso COP= was down 0.2% ahead of Friday's local central bank decision, where it is widely expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points to 12.50%.

On the equity front, Mexican equities .MXX lost 0.6%. Wal-Mart de México WALMEX.MX, Walmart's Mexican arm, slipped 1.4% after the retailer missed third-quarter profit estimates.

In Chile, the peso CLP= slipped 0.4%, while stocks .MMXIPSAGC fell 0.8% after the central bank held its benchmark interest rate at 4.5% on Tuesday, in line with analysts' expectations.

Earlier this month, Chile cut its economic growth forecast for the year while slightly raising its inflation outlook.

FEMSA UBD has moved into a quieter phase after Tuesday's third-quarter earnings release, with the lending market unwinding sharply and the short score settling at its lowest level in two weeks.

The most striking shift in the data this week is in the cost to borrow, which has fallen from a brief spike to near-normalcy with unusual speed. CTB hit 8.66% on October 2, then climbed back to 3.75% in early October before collapsing to 0.83% by October 27. That is a round-trip of almost the entire spike within a month. The move almost certainly reflects short positioning that was built ahead of earnings and then unwound after the print. Availability remains extremely loose, with far more shares available to borrow than are currently out on loan, so there is no structural tightness in the lending pool. Borrowing FEMSA is effectively free at current rates.

The ORTEX short score, which had briefly touched 26.4 on October 14 during the pre-earnings short build described in last week's note, has now retreated to 25.6. That is a low reading, consistent with the picture of minimal bearish conviction. Short interest was building fast in the days before Tuesday's print: the October 28 earnings-preview note flagged a 23% single-session jump on October 26. What the current data shows is that the borrow market has since normalised, suggesting at least some of that positioning has been covered or rolled off.

The earnings event itself produced a reaction. The most recent historical data point in the snapshot shows the July 28 Q2 print prompted a 8.2% one-day fall and a 5.9% decline over the following five days. The Q3 release on October 27 does not yet carry a recorded post-print move in the structured data, but the stock closed at MXN 231.77 on October 27, down 0.33% on the day and down 2.4% on the week. That modest weekly decline is broadly consistent with a market that was not caught badly offside, though the full picture will only emerge over the next few sessions.

Among correlated peers, KOF (Coca-Cola FEMSA, the bottling subsidiary in which FEMSA holds a stake) fell 3.9% on the week, a softer read than the parent. CCH (Coca-Cola HBC) gained 2.5% over the same period, pulling in the opposite direction. COKE dropped 3.1%. The divergence between the European-listed Coke bottlers, which held up or gained, and the Latin American names, which gave ground, broadly tracks the currency and macro backdrop rather than anything company-specific to FEMSA.

The insider data from the vendor table remains stale, with the most recent recorded trade dated June 10, 2026, and the 90-day net figure of roughly USD 4.6 million in net sales reflecting a director's programme of disposals through March. Nothing in the current data changes that picture.

The next scheduled earnings event is February 23, 2027. Between now and then, the key variable to track is whether borrow costs drift back toward the pre-earnings spike level or continue to normalise lower, which would confirm that the short thesis accumulated in October has been largely abandoned.

Oct 27, 2026

Fomento Economico Mexicano (NYSE:FMX) reported third-quarter 2026 revenue growth of 9.8% and operating income growth of 9.9%, supported by results at OXXO México and Coca-Cola FEMSA, while management highlighted an improving traffic trend at its Mexican convenience-store chain.

Net consolidated income totaled MXN 10.6 billion, up 81% from a year earlier. CFO Martín Arias said the increase reflected operational performance, a favorable comparison with a prior-year loss from discontinued logistics operations, and a MXN 1.1 billion non-cash foreign-exchange gain. Those factors were partly offset by lower interest income, losses on financial instruments at Coca-Cola FEMSA Brazil, and a higher income-tax provision.

On a comparable, currency-neutral basis, FEMSA said revenue increased 9.4% and operating income rose 13.4%.

OXXO México Traffic Gains Momentum

CEO José Antonio Fernández Garza said OXXO Méxicos same-store sales increased 9.2% during the quarter, driven by a 5.5% increase in average ticket and a 3.5% gain in average traffic. Traffic growth was 150 basis points above the second-quarter level, despite limited benefit from the World Cup, he said.

Fernández Garza characterized traffic as the quarters main highlight, noting that average-ticket growth was nominal and included the effects of higher excise taxes on soft drinks and cigarettes. He said OXXO gained market share across relevant trade channels through August, particularly in its core impulse categories.

The company attributed the improvement to its strategy focused on four areas: impulse purchases, food service, daily replenishment, and services. Food-service traffic grew at a low double-digit rate, led by coffee, while early tests of the companys Canasta OXXO offering of everyday essentials at accessible prices were modestly additive to traffic, management said.

OXXO México revenue grew 10.3%, while operating income rose 5.8%. Operating margin contracted 40 basis points. Gross margin declined 120 basis points, although management said the comparison was affected by an unusually high concentration of commercial income in the prior-year period. On a normalized basis, gross-margin contraction would have been in line with the 70-basis-point decline in the second quarter, according to the company.

OXXO México closed 140 older underperforming stores during the quarter as part of a broader pruning plan involving about 250 locations. The closures reduced operating margin by roughly 20 basis points; excluding the effect, operating income would have increased 8%, Arias said. FEMSA expects a similar impact in the fourth quarter as it completes the effort.

Year to date, OXXO México added 734 stores and closed 272, for a net increase of 462 stores. Arias said the company will likely fall short of its annual run rate of 1,000 net new stores this year, but maintained that target for next year and beyond.

Expansion Plans for Bara and International Operations

Bara, FEMSAs discount-store format, delivered same-store sales growth of 10.3% and added 112 net new locations in the quarter. Fernández Garza said newer stores are maturing faster than legacy locations in the Bajío region, while the company expects to open more stores next year than it does this year.

Management described Bara as a major expansion priority, with Investor Relations Director Juan Fonseca saying its store base could grow more than 30% next year. The company said its focus is on improving private-label offerings, simplifying assortments, and building a cost-efficient operating model. Arias said newer Bara stores have reached break-even quickly even before reaching full maturity.

In Latin America, the Americas & Mobility segment generated MXN 29.5 billion in revenue, up 18.1%, or 10.9% on a comparable, currency-neutral basis. The company cited healthy volume growth at OXXO Gas and strong performance in Colombia, where mature-store traffic rose at a high single-digit pace.

OXXO Brazil posted a 5.1% increase in currency-neutral same-store sales, though the operation continued to weigh on consolidated profitability. Management said Brazil remains a significant opportunity but that expansion will be more cautious as the company navigates a 40-hour workweek and two-day-off requirements. FEMSA plans to add about 70 net new Brazilian stores next year, or roughly more than one per week.

Colombia, meanwhile, is ready for faster expansion, Fernández Garza said, provided the company can maintain store quality and operational capabilities.

Other Divisions Face Mixed Conditions

FEMSAs Europe division reported revenue of MXN 14.1 billion, down 5.2% year over year but up 4% on a currency-neutral basis. Swiss retail performed solidly, while German retail and food service were affected by train-route closures and extreme weather that hurt train-station traffic. Operating income fell 24.8% to MXN 531 million.

The health division posted revenue of MXN 22.9 billion, up 7%, though operating income declined 63.2% to MXN 319 million. The results included an additional MXN 430 million non-cash credit-risk provision tied to uncertainty in Colombias healthcare system and the companys institutional-business exposure. Excluding that provision, operating income was MXN 749 million, down 14%, with pressure from competitive initiatives in Chile partly offset by retail growth in Colombia and Ecuador.

Coca-Cola FEMSA reported 10.9% revenue growth and a 15.4% increase in operating income. Arias said operating income would have increased 7.4% excluding a one-time insurance-claim benefit. Mexico volumes remained resilient after the impact of excise-tax increases, while Colombia and Brazil delivered robust volume growth and double-digit operating-income growth.

Capital Allocation and Outlook

FEMSA deployed MXN 9.4 billion in capital expenditures during the quarter, equal to about 4% of revenue and down 28.3% from a year earlier, primarily because Coca-Cola FEMSA reduced spending after prior investments to expand capacity.

The company also announced a new share-repurchase program, in addition to approximately MXN 41 billion in ordinary and extraordinary dividends planned for the current distribution cycle. FEMSA said it has distributed MXN 30 billion of that amount, with the remaining MXN 11 billion expected early next year.

Net debt to EBITDA excluding Coca-Cola FEMSA was 1.19 times at quarter-end, or about 1.3 times on a pro forma basis after accounting for dividend payments. The company maintained its leverage objective of approximately two times net debt to adjusted EBITDA excluding Coca-Cola FEMSA.

Management said it remains encouraged by momentum across most businesses but continues to see a soft consumer environment in Mexico, volatility in Brazil, and increasingly difficult comparisons ahead. FEMSA plans to provide more details about its 2027 plans during its next earnings call.

About Fomento Economico Mexicano (NYSE:FMX)

Fomento Económico Mexicano, SAB. de C.V. (FEMSA) is a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational company with operations focused on beverage bottling, retail and related consumer services. The company traces its origins to 1890, when it was established as a brewery in Monterrey, and has since developed into one of Latin America's largest consumer-facing businesses.

FEMSA's principal beverage business is Coca-Cola FEMSA, which produces, markets, sells and distributes Coca-Cola trademark beverages and other nonalcoholic drinks.

The company also announced a new share-repurchase program, in addition to approximately MXN 41 billion in ordinary and extraordinary dividends planned for the current distribution cycle. FEMSA said it has distributed MXN 30 billion of that amount, with the remaining MXN 11 billion expected early next year.

Net debt to EBITDA excluding Coca-Cola FEMSA was 1.19 times at quarter-end, or about 1.3 times on a pro forma basis after accounting for dividend payments. The company maintained its leverage objective of approximately two times net debt to adjusted EBITDA excluding Coca-Cola FEMSA.

Management said it remains encouraged by momentum across most businesses but continues to see a soft consumer environment in Mexico, volatility in Brazil, and increasingly difficult comparisons ahead. FEMSA plans to provide more details about its 2027 plans during its next earnings call.

About Fomento Economico Mexicano (NYSE:FMX)

Fomento Económico Mexicano, SAB. de C.V. (FEMSA) is a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational company with operations focused on beverage bottling, retail and related consumer services. The company traces its origins to 1890, when it was established as a brewery in Monterrey, and has since developed into one of Latin America's largest consumer-facing businesses.

FEMSA's principal beverage business is Coca-Cola FEMSA, which produces, markets, sells and distributes Coca-Cola trademark beverages and other nonalcoholic drinks.

BOGOTÁ, 28 oct (Reuters) - La Cámara de Representantes de Colombia negó el miércoles cambios a un paquete de artículos específicos de una reforma pensional que habían sido retornados al legislativo por la Corte Constitucional para que corrigieran vicios de procedimiento.

La Corte Constitucional aprobó en agosto la mayor parte de la reforma al sistema de pensional de 2024.

Con esta decisión de la Cámara de Representantes, se acoge el texto de los artículos que habían sido aprobados por el Senado y la Corte Constitucional tendrá que definir si queda corregido el vicio por el cuál se devolvieron los escritos.

La reforma pensional busca fortalecer a la administradora estatal Colpensiones, reducir los subsidios a las altas jubilaciones, entregar beneficios a las mujeres con hijos y ampliar la cobertura para proteger a los adultos mayores en situación de pobreza.

La iniciativa mantiene en 62 años la edad de pensión para los hombres con 1.300 semanas de cotización y en 57 años para las mujeres, aunque reduce el requisito a 850 semanas en casos especiales según el número de hijos.

La reforma también obliga a todos los colombianos que ganan hasta 2,3 salarios mínimos mensuales, unos cuatro millones de pesos (1.317 dólares), a realizar sus aportes de pensión a Colpensiones.

Además, establece que los trabajadores que no lograron cotizar suficientes semanas para una pensión accederán a un beneficio económico, mientras que las personas en situación de pobreza o vulnerabilidad que no aportaron al sistema recibirán mensualmente una renta de unos 75 dólares.

El Gobierno del expresidente izquierdista Gustavo Petro, que impulsó la reforma, estimó que más de 2,6 millones de adultos mayores se beneficiarán de las medidas solidarias.

Los hombres con 900 semanas cotizadas y las mujeres con 750 continuarán en el sistema actual y no estarán obligados a aportar al fondo estatal.

El Gobierno del presidente Abelardo De La Espriella, quien asumió el 7 de agosto, busca consolidar una mayoría en el legislativo donde el partido izquierdista Pacto Histórico tiene la mayor cantidad de congresistas.

La reforma es uno de los cambios de política social más significativos de Colombia en años, según analistas, quienes destacan que ampliará el papel del Estado en el sistema de pensiones, mientras que preserva un rol para los fondos privados, un tema que por mucho tiempo ha dividido a legisladores, empresas y sindicatos.

(Reporte de Carlos Vargas y Nelson Bocanegra)

(( Nelson.bocanegra@thomsonreuters.com ; +571-5185380; Reuters Messaging: Nelson.bocanegra.reuters.net@reuters.com ))

Oct 28, 2026

EFE Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has asked Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori to deepen regional integration through a new development model built around protecting the Amazon and its indigenous peoples,reported on October 27.

The exchange came shortly after Lula won re-election in Brazil's presidential runoff. He took 52% of the vote against 48% for far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a margin of roughly 4.4mn votes. Brazil and Peru share the Amazon rainforest and will mark 200 years of diplomatic relations in 2027.

Lula posted his message on X on October 26, replying to Fujimori's official account. He said the two countries could strengthen regional integration through a sustainable and inclusive form of development that combines conservation of the rainforest with its sustainable use. He added that this approach should recognise the role of indigenous peoples and local communities.

Lula thanked Fujimori for her congratulations, which she had posted on X on October 25, soon after his victory was confirmed. He said he looked forward to celebrating two centuries of partnership between Brazil and Peru in 2027.

In her own post, the right-wing Peruvian leader congratulated Lula on his second-round win and restated her readiness to strengthen the alliance between the two nations. She noted that the bicentenary of bilateral diplomatic ties, first established in February 1827, was approaching. Fujimori said she remained committed to advancing integration, cooperation and sustainable development in the Amazon region the countries share, for the benefit of both peoples.

Bolsonaro had finished first in the opening round of the election with 47% of the vote, two percentage points ahead of Lula.

Oct 28, 2026

Reuters Operations at Antamina, a copper mine in Peru, have been suspended following an accident at its Yanacancha site in which a worker died, according to an October 27 report by. The mine, whose co-owners are Mitsubishi Corp (TYO: 8058), Teck (TSX: TECK.B), Glencore (LON: GLEN) and BHP (ASX: BHP), characterized the stoppage as a precaution.

Antamina is one of the largest copper-silver-zinc mines in the world and a cornerstone of copper mining in Peru, which ranks third globally in production of the metal. The shutdown is a fresh blow to an operation that saw output drop 9% last year after an earlier fatal accident at the site. Copper production at the mine had been recovering in 2026 before the latest halt.

The company said the victim was an operations worker. It has opened an investigation into the death and is cooperating with the authorities.

Reuters Speaking to, a person with close ties to the company said there is still no fixed date for work to restart while the investigation goes on.

Oct 28, 2026

Chilean President José Antonio Kast has committed to attending the inauguration of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Chile's government said, even as Brazil's defeated runoff candidate Flavio Bolsonaro sought to contest the result before fleeing to the US on October 27.

Government undersecretary-general Gonzalo Arenas, of the Segegob, said Kast had given Lula his word that he would take part in the handover ceremony. Lula, of the Workers' Party, is due to begin a fourth term as Brazil's president in January 2027, according to the result certified by the Superior Electoral Court. Bolsonaro initially sought to challenge it, questioning a court decision that extended voting hours in certain areas of the country. His PL party eventually conceded to Lula late on October 26, and Bolsonaro fled to the US via Argentina the following day.

Asked whether Santiago still recognised Lula as the winner of the runoff despite Bolsonaro's request for annulment, Arenas said the government respects the institutions of other countries. 'The institutions have declared President Lula the winner, and therefore we have no other comment to make. We will not get involved in Brazil's internal politics,' he said.

Arenas described Brazil as an ally and a fundamental partner of Chile. 'Whoever the president is, our relations will continue to be state to state,' he said.

The ceremony has traditionally been held on January 1 of the year the term begins. This time, for the first time, it will take place on January 5.

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. The company operates in key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Guatemala, utilizing an extensive supply chain and distribution network to reach consumers efficiently. Among its fastest-growing segments are still beverages, particularly flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, fueled by rising demand for healthier and functional options amid shifting consumer preferences. This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

8.1 Activities

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. The company operates in key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Guatemala, utilizing an extensive supply chain and distribution network to reach consumers efficiently. Among its fastest-growing segments are still beverages, particularly flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, fueled by rising demand for healthier and functional options amid shifting consumer preferences. This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Kimberly-Clark de Mexico S.A. de C.V., a subsidiary of the global Kimberly-Clark Corporation, is a leading manufacturer and marketer of personal care and consumer tissue products in Mexico. The company specializes in producing a diverse portfolio of essential items, including baby diapers, feminine hygiene products, facial tissues, toilet paper, and professional wipes for healthcare and industrial applications. Its operations emphasize innovation, sustainability, and efficient supply chain management to serve both domestic and international markets. Among its fastest-growing segments are premium personal care products, such as advanced incontinence and feminine care solutions, fueled by rising consumer demand for high-quality, eco-friendly options and expanding e-commerce channels. Additionally, the professional segment, particularly wipes and protective gear, has seen strong growth due to increased adoption in healthcare and workplace safety sectors, positioning the company for continued market expansion in Latin America. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 20th largest Health care company by market capitalization.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Kimberly-Clark de Mexico S.A. de C.V., a subsidiary of the global Kimberly-Clark Corporation, is a leading manufacturer and marketer of personal care and consumer tissue products in Mexico. The company specializes in producing a diverse portfolio of essential items, including baby diapers, feminine hygiene products, facial tissues, toilet paper, and professional wipes for healthcare and industrial applications. Its operations emphasize innovation, sustainability, and efficient supply chain management to serve both domestic and international markets. Among its fastest-growing segments are premium personal care products, such as advanced incontinence and feminine care solutions, fueled by rising consumer demand for high-quality, eco-friendly options and expanding e-commerce channels. Additionally, the professional segment, particularly wipes and protective gear, has seen strong growth due to increased adoption in healthcare and workplace safety sectors, positioning the company for continued market expansion in Latin America. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 20th largest Health care company by market capitalization.

MEXICO CITY--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: VTMX; BMV: VESTA) ("Vesta" or the "Company"), a leading industrial real estate company in Mexico, today announced that it will host its 2026 Investor Day on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, in New York, NY.

At the event, Vesta's management team will discuss the Company's business performance, capital allocation priorities, and long-term growth outlook with important updates related to the Company's Route 2030 strategic plan, including recent development projects across key markets and other initiatives driving long-term value creation.

On-site registration and networking breakfast with management will begin at 8:00 a.m. ET, followed by management presentations at 9:00 a.m. ET and a live Q&A session with members of the management team.

The event is open to institutional investors and sell-side analysts and will be available both in person and via live webcast. Pre-registration is required by November 3, 2026.

To register, please visit vestaday.com. Due to limited capacity, in-person attendance is subject to confirmation, and confirmed attendees will receive additional event details. A live webcast, replay and presentation materials will be available through Vesta's Investor Relations website at ir.vesta.com.mx following the event.

May 26, 2026: Vesta Announces Two New Lease Agreements Totaling More Than 570 Thousand Square Feet in Monterrey

MEXICO CITY--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta, S.A.B. de C.V. ("Vesta" or the "Company") (NYSE: VTMX; BMV: VESTA), a fully-integrated, internally managed real estate company that owns, manages, develops and leases industrial properties in Mexico, announced that it has entered into two new lease agreements for a total of more than 570 thousand square feet in Monterrey, reflecting the continued progress on the Company's Route 2030 strategic growth plan.

At Vesta Park Apodaca, one of the industrial parks with the best connectivity and building quality in Monterrey, Vesta leased two buildings to European companies specializing in industrial manufacturing and the production of industrial equipment linked to critical infrastructure and specialized supply chains.

These operations will strengthen the region's industrial ecosystem and contribute to the growth of strategic sectors in North America, particularly those related to the expansion of data center infrastructure.

"We are very pleased with the demand for space we are seeing related to the data center sector in North America. At Vesta, we will continue to serve the fastest-growing industries," said Mario Chacon, Vesta's Chief Commercial Officer.

With these transactions, Vesta continues to consolidate its position as one of the leading developers of industrial infrastructure in Mexico, driving projects aligned with the trends of digitalization, nearshoring and expansion of industrial capabilities in the region.

Source: Company Website

MEXICO CITY--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Corporacion Inmobiliaria Vesta, S.A.B. de C.V. ("Vesta") (NYSE: VTMX; BMV: VESTA), a fully-integrated, internally managed real estate company that owns, manages, develops and leases industrial properties in Mexico, today announced the closing of its global offering of 1,199,285 American Depositary Shares, or ADS, at a price of US$34.62 per ADS in the United States (the "International Offering") and 58,054,784 common shares at a price of Ps.$59.50 per common share in Mexico (the "Mexican Offering", and together with the International Offering, the "Global Offering"). Each ADS represents 10 common shares of Vesta. The underlying common shares are registered in the Mexican National Securities Registry (Registro Nacional de Valores; the "RNV"), which is maintained by the Mexican National Banking and Securities Commission (Comision Nacional Bancaria y de Valores; the "CNBV").

The international underwriters have been granted a 30-day option to purchase up to 10,507,140 additional common shares represented by ADSs. Any common shares represented by ADSs sold under the option will be sold on the same terms and conditions as the initial common shares represented by ADSs, that are the subject of the International Offering.

The gross proceeds were approximately US$242.5 million. Vesta intends to use the net proceeds from the offering to fund its growth strategy, as described in its prospectus supplement.

Barclays, J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley are acting as joint global coordinators of this offering. BofA Securities, BTG Pactual and Santander are acting as joint book-runners.

The International Offering in the United States and elsewhere (outside Mexico) was made only by means of a prospectus and a prospectus supplement.
